sentences.zh: 李綱李綱，字文紀，觀州蓚人也。

translations.literal: Li Gang—Li Gang, styled Wenji, was a native of Zhuo in Guanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang, styled Wenji, came from Zhuo in Guanzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖元則，後魏清河太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yuanze was prefect of Qinghe under the Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yuanze had served as prefect of Qinghe under the Later Wei.

sentences.zh: 父制，周車騎大將軍。

translations.literal: His father Zhi was Grand General of Cavalry under the Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhi had been Grand General of Cavalry under Northern Zhou.

sentences.zh: 綱少慷慨有志節，每以忠義自許。

translations.literal: Gang in his youth was ardent and possessed integrity of purpose, and constantly pledged himself to loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Gang was ardent and high-minded, and he constantly held himself to a standard of loyalty and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 初名瑗，字子玉，讀《後漢書·張綱傳》，慕而改之。

translations.literal: His original name was Yuan, styled Ziyu; after reading the biography of Zhang Gang in the Book of the Later Han, he admired him and changed his name accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: He had first been named Yuan, styled Ziyu; after reading the biography of Zhang Gang in the Book of the Later Han, he admired the man and took Gang as his name.

sentences.zh: 周齊王憲引為參軍。

translations.literal: The Zhou Prince of Qi, Xian, recruited him as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Zhou Prince of Qi, Xian, took him on as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 宣帝將害憲，召僚屬證成其罪，綱誓之以死，終無撓辭。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan was about to destroy Xian, he summoned his subordinates to testify to his crimes; Gang pledged himself to death and in the end never yielded in his words.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan was about to destroy Xian, he summoned his staff to testify to Xian's crimes; Gang swore he would die rather than comply, and in the end never wavered in what he said.

sentences.zh: 及憲遇害，露車載屍而出，故吏皆散，唯綱撫棺號慟，躬自埋瘞，哭拜而去。

translations.literal: When Xian met his death, his body was carried out on an open cart; his former subordinates all scattered—only Gang caressed the coffin and wailed, personally buried him, and departed after bowing in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian was killed, his body was carried out on an open cart and his former officers all scattered; only Gang clung to the coffin and wailed, buried the body himself, and left after bowing in grief.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇末，為太子洗馬。

translations.literal: At the end of the Kaihuang era of Sui, he served as Academician to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Sui Kaihuang era he served as Academician to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 皇太子勇嘗以歲首宴宮臣，左庶子唐令則自請奏琵琶，又歌《武媚娘》之曲。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Yong once held a New Year's banquet for palace officials; the Left Assistant Censor Tang Lingze volunteered to play the pipa and also sang the tune "Lady Wumei."
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Yong once held a New Year's banquet for his palace staff; the Left Assistant Censor Tang Lingze volunteered to play the pipa and also sang the tune "Lady Wumei."

sentences.zh: 綱自勇曰：「令則身任宮卿，職當調護，乃於宴座自比倡優，進淫聲，穢視聽。

translations.literal: Gang addressed Yong directly: "Lingze holds the post of palace counselor and his duty is to oversee regulation—yet at the banquet he compares himself to entertainers, presents licentious music, and defiles what eyes and ears should behold.
translations.idiomatic: Gang spoke to Yong himself: "Lingze holds a palace counselor's post and his duty is to oversee your conduct—yet at this banquet he compares himself to entertainers, offers licentious music, and defiles what your eyes and ears should take in.

sentences.zh: 事若上聞，令則罪不測，豈不累於殿下？

translations.literal: If this matter reaches the sovereign, Lingze's offense cannot be measured—will this not bring ruin upon Your Highness?
translations.idiomatic: If the emperor hears of this, Lingze's offense cannot be foreseen—will that not bring disaster upon Your Highness as well?

sentences.zh: 臣請遽正其罪。」

translations.literal: Your servant requests that his crime be promptly corrected."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that his offense be corrected at once."

sentences.zh: 勇曰：「我欲為樂耳，君勿多事。」

translations.literal: Yong said: "I merely wished for amusement—do not meddle so much."
translations.idiomatic: Yong said: "I only wanted some amusement—do not make so much of it."

sentences.zh: 綱趨而出。

translations.literal: Gang rushed out.
translations.idiomatic: Gang strode out at once.

sentences.zh: 及勇廢黜，文帝召東宮官屬切讓之，無敢對者。

translations.literal: When Yong was deposed, Emperor Wen summoned the Eastern Palace officials and reproached them sharply; none dared reply.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong was deposed, Emperor Wen summoned the Eastern Palace staff and rebuked them harshly; no one dared answer.

sentences.zh: 綱對曰：「今日之事，乃陛下之過，非太子罪也。

translations.literal: Gang replied: "Today's affair is the fault of Your Majesty, not the crime of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Gang replied: "What has happened today is Your Majesty's fault, not the Crown Prince's crime.

sentences.zh: 勇器非上品，性是常人，若得賢明之士輔導之，足堪繼嗣皇業。

translations.literal: Yong's capacity was not of the highest rank and his nature that of an ordinary man—had worthy and enlightened men guided him, he would fully have sufficed to inherit the imperial enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's talents were not of the highest order and his nature was that of an ordinary man; had worthy and enlightened men guided him, he would have been fully adequate to inherit the imperial enterprise.

sentences.zh: 方今多士盈朝，當擇賢者居其任，奈何以絃歌鷹犬之才侍側，至令致此？

translations.literal: Now scholars crowd the court; one ought to place the worthy in their posts—how can one set beside him men skilled only in song and hawking, so that matters come to this?
translations.idiomatic: Scholars now fill the court; the worthy ought to be placed in office—how could men skilled only in song and hawking be kept at his side until things came to this?

sentences.zh: 乃陛下訓導不足，豈太子之罪耶！」

translations.literal: It is insufficient instruction and guidance on Your Majesty's part—how could it be the Crown Prince's crime!"
translations.idiomatic: It is that Your Majesty's instruction and guidance were insufficient—how could it be the Crown Prince's crime!"

sentences.zh: 辭氣凜然，左右皆為之失色。

translations.literal: His tone was stern and awesome; those on left and right all turned pale on his account.
translations.idiomatic: His words were stern and commanding; those at his side all turned pale because of him.

sentences.zh: 文帝曰：「令汝在彼，豈非擇人？」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen said: "Appointing you there—was that not selecting a man?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen said: "Sending you there—was that not choosing a man?"

sentences.zh: 綱曰：「臣在東宮，非得言者。」

translations.literal: Gang said: "When I was in the Eastern Palace, I had no one who would speak out."
translations.idiomatic: Gang said: "In the Eastern Palace I had no one who was permitted to speak frankly."

sentences.zh: 帝奇其對，擢拜尚書右丞。

translations.literal: The emperor marveled at his reply and promoted him to Vice Director in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was struck by his answer and promoted him to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時左僕射楊素、蘇威當朝用事，綱每固執所見，不與之同，由是二人深惡之。

translations.literal: At the time the Left Director Yang Su and Su Wei held power in the court; Gang constantly held to his own views and would not agree with them, whereupon the two deeply hated him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Left Directors Yang Su and Su Wei dominated the court; Gang constantly held to his own views and would not go along with them, and the two came to hate him deeply.

sentences.zh: 會遣大將軍劉方誅討林邑，楊素言於文帝曰：「林邑多珍寶，自非正人不可委。」

translations.literal: When it happened that the general Liu Fang was sent to campaign against Linyi, Yang Su said to Emperor Wen: "Linyi has many precious things—only an upright man may be entrusted with it."
translations.idiomatic: When the great general Liu Fang was sent to campaign against Linyi, Yang Su told Emperor Wen: "Linyi holds many precious goods; only an upright man may be entrusted with such a post."

sentences.zh: 因言綱可任，文帝以為行軍司馬。

translations.literal: He therefore said Gang could take the post; the emperor made him campaigning staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: He then said Gang was fit for the duty, and the emperor appointed him campaigning staff officer.

sentences.zh: 劉方承素之意，屈辱綱，幾至於死。

translations.literal: Liu Fang, following Su's intent, humiliated Gang, nearly to the point of death.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang, carrying out Su's intent, humiliated Gang almost to the point of death.

sentences.zh: 及軍還，久不得調。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he long went without reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he went for a long time without a new appointment.

sentences.zh: 後拜齊王府司馬。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed secretary in the household of the Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed secretary in the household of the Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 未幾，蘇威復令綱詣南海應接林邑，久而不召。

translations.literal: Before long Su Wei again sent Gang to the Southern Sea to liaison with Linyi; for a long time he was not recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Su Wei again sent Gang to the Southern Sea to handle affairs with Linyi, and for a long time did not summon him back.

sentences.zh: 綱後自來奏事，威復言綱擅離所職，以之屬吏。

translations.literal: When Gang later came on his own to present matters, Su again charged that Gang had left his post without authorization and handed him over to the officials.
translations.idiomatic: When Gang later came on his own to report to court, Su again accused him of leaving his post without leave and handed him over to the judicial officers.

sentences.zh: 綱見善卜者，令筮之，遇《鼎》，因謂綱曰：「公易姓之後，方可得志而為卿輔。

translations.literal: Gang saw a man skilled in divination and had him cast the hexagram; he obtained Ding, and the diviner therefore told Gang: "After the lord changes his surname, he may then realize his ambition and serve as minister to the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Gang met a skilled diviner and had him cast the hexagram; the result was Ding, and the man therefore told Gang: "Only after the ruling house changes its surname will you realize your ambition and serve as a minister to the throne.

sentences.zh: 宜早退；

translations.literal: You ought to withdraw early;
translations.idiomatic: You ought to withdraw early;

sentences.zh: 不然，有折足之敗也。」

translations.literal: otherwise there will be the disaster of a broken leg."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise you will meet the disaster of a broken leg."

sentences.zh: 尋會赦免，屏居於鄠。

translations.literal: Before long he encountered an amnesty and was released; he withdrew to live in seclusion at E.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an amnesty was declared and he was released; he withdrew to live in seclusion at E.

sentences.zh: 大業末，賊帥何潘仁以綱為長史。

translations.literal: Near the end of the Daye era, the rebel leader He Panren made him chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daye era, the rebel leader He Panren appointed him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 義師至京城，綱來謁見。

translations.literal: When the righteous army reached the capital, Gang came to pay his respects.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army reached the capital, Gang came to pay his respects.

sentences.zh: 高祖大悅，授丞相府司錄，封新昌縣公，專掌選。

translations.literal: Gaozu was greatly pleased, appointed him Registrar in the Chancellor's Office, enfeoffed him as Duke of Xinchang, and put him solely in charge of selection.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was greatly pleased, appointed him Registrar in the Chancellor's Office, enfeoffed him as Duke of Xinchang, and put him solely in charge of official selection.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐祚，拜禮部尚書，兼太子詹事，典選如故。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, he was appointed Minister of Rites and concurrently Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent, with charge of selection as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, he was appointed Minister of Rites and concurrently Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent, with charge of selection unchanged.

sentences.zh: 先是，巢王元吉授并州總管，於是縱其左右攘奪百姓，宇文歆頻諫不納，乃上表曰：「王在州之日，多出微行，常共竇誕遊獵，蹂踐谷稼，放縱親暱，公行攘奪，境內獸畜，取之殆盡。

translations.literal: Before this, Prince Yuanji of Qi had been appointed commander at Bingzhou; there he allowed his attendants to seize from the common people. Yuwen Xin repeatedly remonstrated without acceptance, and therefore submitted a memorial saying: "When the prince was in the prefecture he often went out incognito, regularly hunted with Dou Dan, trampled grain in the fields, indulged his intimates, openly seized by force, until the livestock within the borders were nearly all taken.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Prince Yuanji of Qi had been made commander at Bingzhou, where he allowed his attendants to plunder the people. Yuwen Xin remonstrated again and again without being heeded and therefore submitted a memorial: "While the prince was in the prefecture he often went out incognito, regularly went hunting with Dou Dan, trampled the grain in the fields, indulged his favorites, and openly seized property by force until the livestock within the borders were nearly exhausted.

sentences.zh: 當衢而射，觀人避箭以為笑樂。

translations.literal: He shot in the public thoroughfare and took people's dodging his arrows for a jest.
translations.idiomatic: He shot arrows in the public streets and took people's scrambling to avoid them as a source of amusement.

sentences.zh: 分遣左右，戲為攻戰，至相擊刺疻傷致死。

translations.literal: He sent his attendants to play at warfare, until they stabbed each other and died of their wounds.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his attendants to play at warfare until they stabbed one another and some died of their wounds.

sentences.zh: 夜開府門，宣淫他室。

translations.literal: At night he opened the government gate and debauched other men's households.
translations.idiomatic: At night he opened the government gate and debauched other men's households.

sentences.zh: 百姓怨毒，各懷憤嘆。

translations.literal: The people harbored poisoned resentment, each filled with angry lament.
translations.idiomatic: The common people were filled with bitter resentment, each nursing angry grief.

sentences.zh: 以此守城，安能自保！」

translations.literal: With such a man defending a city, how could he protect himself!"
translations.idiomatic: With such conduct, how could he defend a city and keep himself safe!"

sentences.zh: 元吉竟坐免。

translations.literal: Yuanji in the end was removed from office on account of it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji was in the end dismissed from office on account of this.

sentences.zh: 又諷父老詣闕請之，尋令復職。

translations.literal: They also prompted the elders to go to the court to request his return; before long he was ordered to resume his post.
translations.idiomatic: They also prompted the local elders to go to court and request his return; before long he was ordered to resume his duties.

sentences.zh: 時劉武週率五千騎至黃蛇嶺，元吉遣車騎將軍張達以步卒百人先嘗之。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Wuzhou led five thousand horsemen to Huangshe Ridge; Yuanji sent the General of Chariots and Cavalry Zhang Da with a hundred foot soldiers to probe them first.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Wuzhou led five thousand horsemen to Huangshe Ridge; Yuanji sent the General of Chariots and Cavalry Zhang Da with a hundred foot soldiers to test the enemy first.

sentences.zh: 達以步卒少，固請不行。

translations.literal: Da, seeing the infantry too few, firmly requested not to go.
translations.idiomatic: Da, seeing the infantry too few, firmly refused to go.

sentences.zh: 元吉強遣之，至則盡沒於賊。

translations.literal: Yuanji forced him to go; upon arrival they were all lost to the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji forced him to go anyway; upon arrival they were all wiped out by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 達憤怒，因引武周攻陷榆次，進逼并州。

translations.literal: In anger Da therefore led Wuzhou to storm and take Yuci and press on toward Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In fury Da then guided Wuzhou to storm and take Yuci and advance on Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 元吉大懼，紿其司馬劉德威曰：「卿以老弱守城，吾以強兵出戰。」

translations.literal: Yuanji was greatly afraid and deceived his secretary Liu Dewei, saying: "You with the aged and weak defend the city; I with strong troops will go out to battle."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji was terrified and deceived his secretary Liu Dewei, saying: "You with the aged and weak will defend the city; I with strong troops will go out to give battle."

sentences.zh: 因夜出兵，攜其妻孥，棄軍奔還京師，并州遂陷。

translations.literal: That night he led his army out, taking wife and children, abandoned the army and fled back to the capital—Bingzhou was thus lost.
translations.idiomatic: That night he marched his army out, took wife and children with him, abandoned the troops, and fled back to the capital; Bingzhou was thus lost.

sentences.zh: 高祖怒甚，謂綱曰：「元吉幼小，未習時事，故遣竇誕、宇文歆輔之。

translations.literal: Gaozu was exceedingly angry and said to Gang: "Yuanji is still young and unversed in affairs; therefore I sent Dou Dan and Yuwen Xin to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was furious and said to Gang: "Yuanji is still young and unversed in affairs; that is why I sent Dou Dan and Yuwen Xin to assist him.

sentences.zh: 強兵數萬，食支十年，起義興運之資，一朝而棄。

translations.literal: Strong troops in the tens of thousands, provisions to last ten years—the resources for raising righteousness and fortune—cast aside in a single morning.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of strong troops and provisions to last ten years—the resources on which our righteous uprising and good fortune rested—thrown away in a single morning.

sentences.zh: 宇文歆首畫此計，我當斬之。」

translations.literal: Yuwen Xin first devised this plan—I ought to execute him."
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Xin first devised this plan—I ought to execute him."

sentences.zh: 綱曰：「賴歆令陛下不失愛子，臣以為有功。」

translations.literal: Gang said: "It is thanks to Xin that Your Majesty did not lose a beloved son; I consider that a merit."
translations.idiomatic: Gang said: "It is thanks to Xin that Your Majesty did not lose a beloved son; I consider that a merit."

sentences.zh: 高祖問其故，綱對曰：「罪由竇誕不能規諷，致令軍人怨憤。

translations.literal: Gaozu asked the reason; Gang replied: "The crime lay with Dou Dan's failure to admonish and instruct, so that the soldiers grew resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu asked why; Gang replied: "The fault lay with Dou Dan's failure to admonish and instruct, which made the soldiers resentful.

sentences.zh: 又齊王年少，肆行驕逸放縱，左右侵漁百姓，誕曾無諫止，乃隨順掩藏，以成其釁，此誕之罪。

translations.literal: Moreover the Prince of Qi was young and indulged in arrogant, wanton excess; his attendants encroached on the people, yet Dan never remonstrated or stopped it—he only followed along and covered it up, thereby completing the prince's offenses; this was Dan's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Prince of Qi was young and indulged in arrogant excess; his attendants preyed on the people, yet Dan never remonstrated or stopped them—he only followed along and covered matters up, thereby completing the prince's offenses; that was Dan's crime.

sentences.zh: 宇文歆論情則疏，向彼又淺，王之過失，悉以聞奏。

translations.literal: Yuwen Xin by affection was distant and toward the prince was shallow, yet all the prince's faults he entirely reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Xin was distant in personal ties and shallow in his relation to the prince, yet he reported every one of the prince's faults to the throne.

sentences.zh: 且父子之際，人所難言，歆言之，豈非忠懇？

translations.literal: Between father and son it is hard for anyone to speak—when Xin spoke, was that not loyal earnestness?
translations.idiomatic: Between father and son it is what people find hardest to speak of—when Xin spoke out, was that not loyal earnestness?

sentences.zh: 今欲誅罪，不錄其心，臣愚竊以為過。」

translations.literal: To wish to punish him now without recording his heart—I foolishly consider that excessive."
translations.idiomatic: To wish to punish him now without crediting his intent—I humbly consider that excessive."

sentences.zh: 翌日，高祖召綱入，升御坐謂曰：「今我有公，遂使刑罰不濫。

translations.literal: The next day Gaozu summoned Gang in, ascended the imperial seat, and said: "Today I have you, and thus punishments are not abused.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Gaozu summoned Gang in, took the imperial seat, and said: "Now that I have you, punishments are not abused.

sentences.zh: 元吉自惡，結怨於人。

translations.literal: Yuanji brought evil on himself and made enemies among men.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji brought evil on himself and made enemies among men.

sentences.zh: 歆既曾以表聞，誕亦焉能制禁？」

translations.literal: Since Xin had already memorialized, how could Dan have restrained him?"
translations.idiomatic: Since Xin had already memorialized, how could Dan have restrained him?"

sentences.zh: 時高祖拜舞人安叱奴為散騎常侍，綱上疏諫曰：「謹案《周禮》，均工、樂胥不得預於仕伍。

translations.literal: At that time Gaozu enfeoffed the dancer An Chinu as Gentleman Attendant at the Imperial Suite; Gang submitted a memorial remonstrating: "According to the Rites of Zhou, the directors of craftsmen and music masters may not enter the ranks of office.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gaozu appointed the dancer An Chinu Gentleman Attendant at the Imperial Suite; Gang submitted a memorial remonstrating: "According to the Rites of Zhou, directors of craftsmen and music masters may not enter the ranks of office.

sentences.zh: 雖復才如子野，妙等師襄，皆身終子繼，不易其業。

translations.literal: Even if talent matched Ziye and skill equaled Master Xiang, all ended their lives with sons succeeding them and did not change their profession.
translations.idiomatic: Even if one's talent matched Ziye and one's skill equaled Master Xiang, each ended his life with a son succeeding him and did not change his profession.

sentences.zh: 故魏武使祢衡擊鼓，衡先解朝服，露體而擊之，雲不敢以先王法服為伶人之衣。

translations.literal: Therefore Cao Cao had Mi Heng beat the drum; Heng first removed his court robes and, baring his body, beat it, saying he dared not use the ritual garments of former kings as a performer's clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when Cao Cao had Mi Heng beat the drum, Heng first stripped off his court robes and beat it with his body bare, saying he dared not use the ritual garments of former kings as a performer's costume.

sentences.zh: 雖齊高緯封曹妙達為王，授安馬駒為開府，既招物議，大絜彝倫，有國有家者以為殷鑑。

translations.literal: Although Gao Wei of Qi enfeoffed Cao Miaoda as king and appointed An Maju as Director of the Palace, they already drew public censure and greatly disturbed the great norms; those with state and family took this as a warning mirror.
translations.idiomatic: Although Gao Wei of Northern Qi enfeoffed Cao Miaoda as king and appointed An Maju Director of the Palace, they already drew public censure and gravely disturbed the great norms; rulers of states and families have taken this as a warning.

sentences.zh: 方今新定天下，開太平之基。

translations.literal: Now the realm has newly been settled and the foundation of great peace opened.
translations.idiomatic: The realm has only just been settled and the foundation of great peace laid.

sentences.zh: 起義功臣，行賞未遍；

translations.literal: Meritorious men of the righteous uprising have not yet all received rewards;
translations.idiomatic: The meritorious men of the righteous uprising have not yet all been rewarded;

sentences.zh: 高才碩學，猶滯草萊。

translations.literal: men of lofty talent and great learning still linger among the common fields.
translations.idiomatic: men of lofty talent and great learning still linger in obscurity.

sentences.zh: 而先令舞胡，致位五品；

translations.literal: yet you first set a dancing barbarian in a post of the fifth rank;
translations.idiomatic: yet you first set a dancing barbarian in a post of the fifth rank;

sentences.zh: 鳴玉曳組，趨馳廊廟，顧非創業垂統貽厥子孫之道也。」

translations.literal: jingling jade and trailing ribbons, hurrying through the halls of state—this is surely not the way to found an enterprise, hand down a tradition, and bequeath it to one's descendants."
translations.idiomatic: with jade sounding at his belt and official ribbons trailing, rushing through the halls of state—surely this is not the way to found an enterprise, hand down a tradition, and bequeath it to one's descendants."

sentences.zh: 高祖不納。

translations.literal: Gaozu did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu did not accept the advice.

sentences.zh: 尋令參詳律令。

translations.literal: Before long he was ordered to take part in reviewing the statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was ordered to take part in reviewing the statutes and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 綱在東宮，隱太子建成初甚禮遇。

translations.literal: Gang was in the Eastern Palace; the Hidden Heir, Crown Prince Jiancheng, at first treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Gang served in the Eastern Palace; the Hidden Heir, Crown Prince Jiancheng, at first treated him with great courtesy.

sentences.zh: 建成常往溫湯，綱時以疾不從。

translations.literal: Jiancheng often went to the hot springs; Gang at times, owing to illness, did not accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng often went to the hot springs; Gang sometimes, owing to illness, did not go with him.

sentences.zh: 有進生魚於建成者，將召饔人作鱠。

translations.literal: Someone presented live fish to Jiancheng; he was about to summon the cook to prepare it as sashimi.
translations.idiomatic: Someone presented live fish to Jiancheng; he was about to summon the cook to prepare sashimi.

sentences.zh: 時唐儉、趙元楷在座，各自讚能為鱠，建成從之，既而謂曰：「飛刀鱠鯉，調和鼎食，公實有之；

translations.literal: At the time Tang Jian and Zhao Yuankai were seated; each praised his own ability to make sashimi, and Jiancheng followed them; afterward he said: "Flying-knife sashimi of carp and harmonizing the food in the cauldron—you truly have these;
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jian and Zhao Yuankai were present; each praised his own skill at sashimi, and Jiancheng let them do it; afterward he said: "Flying-knife sashimi of carp and harmonizing the food in the cauldron—you truly have these;

sentences.zh: 至於審諭弼諧，固屬於李綱矣。」

translations.literal: as for examining and instructing, assisting and harmonizing, that surely belongs to Li Gang."
translations.idiomatic: as for examining and instructing and assisting in harmony, that surely belongs to Li Gang."

sentences.zh: 於是遣使送絹二百匹以遺之。

translations.literal: He therefore sent an envoy with two hundred bolts of silk as a gift to him.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent an envoy with two hundred bolts of silk as a gift to him.

sentences.zh: 建成後漸狎無行之徒，有猜忌之謀，不可諫止。

translations.literal: Later Jiancheng gradually grew intimate with men of no conduct and harbored schemes of suspicion; he could not be remonstrated with and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jiancheng gradually grew intimate with worthless men and harbored schemes of suspicion; nothing could be said to stop him.

sentences.zh: 又思筮者之言，頻乞骸骨。

translations.literal: Gang also recalled the diviner's words and repeatedly begged to retire on account of age.
translations.idiomatic: Gang also recalled the diviner's words and repeatedly asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 高祖漫罵之曰：「卿為潘仁長史，何乃羞為朕尚書？

translations.literal: Gaozu casually scolded him, saying: "You served as chief clerk to Panren—how can you be ashamed to be my Minister?
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu casually scolded him: "You served as chief clerk to Panren—how can you be ashamed to be my Minister?

sentences.zh: 且建成在東宮，遣卿輔導，何為屢致辭乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover Jiancheng is in the Eastern Palace and I sent you to guide him—why do you repeatedly offer your resignation?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Jiancheng is in the Eastern Palace and I sent you to guide him—why do you keep resigning?"

sentences.zh: 綱頓首陳謝曰：「潘仁，賊也，誠在殺害，每諫便止，所活極多，為其長史，故得無愧。

translations.literal: Gang bowed his head and stated in apology: "Panren was a bandit and truly intended slaughter; each time I remonstrated he stopped, and those saved were extremely many—serving as his chief clerk, I therefore had no shame.
translations.idiomatic: Gang bowed his head and replied: "Panren was a rebel and truly meant to kill; each time I remonstrated he stopped, and an enormous number of lives were saved—serving as his chief clerk, I therefore had nothing to be ashamed of.

sentences.zh: 陛下功成業泰，頗自矜伐，臣以凡劣，才乖元凱，所言如水投石，安敢久為尚書？

translations.literal: Your Majesty's merit is accomplished and enterprise at peace, yet you are rather self-congratulatory; I am commonplace and inferior, my talent falling short of the great ministers—what I say is like water cast on stone—how dare I long remain Minister?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's merit is accomplished and your enterprise secure, yet you are rather self-congratulatory; I am commonplace and my talent falls short of the great ministers—what I say is like water cast on stone—how dare I long remain Minister?

sentences.zh: 兼以愚臣事太子，所懷鄙見，復不探納，既無補益，所以請退。」

translations.literal: Moreover, as a foolish servant attending the Heir Apparent, the humble views I hold are again not taken up; since there is no benefit, I therefore request to withdraw."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, serving the Heir Apparent as a foolish subordinate, the humble views I hold are again not heeded; since I can do no good, I ask to withdraw."

sentences.zh: 高祖謝曰：「知公直士，勉弼我兒。」

translations.literal: Gaozu apologized, saying: "I know you are an upright man—do your best to assist my son."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu apologized: "I know you are an upright man—do your best to assist my son."

sentences.zh: 於是擢拜太子少保，尚書、詹事並如故。

translations.literal: He was therefore promoted to Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent, with his posts as Minister and Grand Mentor unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore promoted to Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent, while his posts as Minister and Grand Mentor remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 綱又上書諫太子曰：「綱耄矣，日過時流，墳樹已拱，幸未就土，許傅聖躬，無以酬恩，請效愚直，伏願殿下詳之。

translations.literal: Gang again submitted a letter remonstrating with the Heir Apparent: "Gang is aged; the days pass and the times flow on; the trees at my grave already arch—fortunately I have not yet entered the earth, yet I am permitted to attend upon your sacred person; I have no means to repay your grace and beg to offer my foolish frankness; I humbly wish Your Highness will consider it carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Gang again submitted a letter remonstrating with the Heir Apparent: "I am old; the days pass and the times flow on; the trees at my grave already arch over it—fortunately I have not yet gone into the earth, yet I am permitted to attend upon your sacred person; I have no way to repay your grace and beg to offer my foolish frankness; I humbly ask Your Highness to consider it carefully.

sentences.zh: 竊見飲酒過多，誠非養生之術。

translations.literal: I have observed that drinking too much wine is truly not the method of nurturing life.
translations.idiomatic: I have observed that drinking too much is truly not the way to nurture one's health.

sentences.zh: 且凡為人子者，務於孝友，以慰君父之心，不宜聽受邪言，妄生猜忌。」

translations.literal: Moreover, all who are sons ought to devote themselves to filial piety and brotherly harmony to comfort the hearts of lord and father; they ought not heed perverse words and rashly harbor suspicion."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, every son ought to devote himself to filial piety and brotherly harmony to comfort his father and sovereign; he ought not heed perverse words and rashly harbor suspicion."

sentences.zh: 建成覽書不懌，而所為如故。

translations.literal: Jiancheng read the letter without pleasure, yet acted as before.
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng read the letter without pleasure, yet continued as before.

sentences.zh: 綱以數言事忤太子旨，道既不行，鬱鬱不得志。

translations.literal: Gang, because he repeatedly spoke on affairs contrary to the Heir Apparent's intent, found his way blocked and grew depressed without realizing his aims.
translations.idiomatic: Because Gang repeatedly spoke on affairs contrary to the Heir Apparent's wishes, his counsel went unheeded and he grew depressed without realizing his aims.

sentences.zh: 武德二年，以老表辭職，優詔解尚書，仍為太子少保。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wude, on account of age he submitted a memorial resigning; an excellent edict released him from the Ministry but kept him as Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wude he submitted a memorial resigning on account of age; an edict graciously released him from the Ministry but kept him as Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 高祖以綱隋代名臣，甚加優禮，每手敕未嘗稱名，其見重如此。

translations.literal: Gaozu, because Gang was a famous minister of the Sui, treated him with great courtesy; in each personal edict he never used his personal name—such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Because Gang had been a famous minister of the Sui, Gaozu treated him with exceptional courtesy; in each personal edict he never used Gang's personal name—such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 貞觀四年，拜太子少師。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenguan, he was appointed Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenguan he was appointed Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 時綱有腳疾，不堪踐履，太宗特賜步輿，令綱乘至閣下，數引入禁中，問以政道。

translations.literal: At the time Gang had a foot ailment and could not walk; Taizong specially granted him a sedan chair and ordered Gang to ride it to below the pavilion; he was repeatedly brought into the inner palace to be asked about governance.
translations.idiomatic: Gang then suffered from a foot ailment and could not walk; Taizong specially granted him a sedan chair and had him ride it to the steps of the hall, and repeatedly brought him into the inner palace to question him on the way of government.

sentences.zh: 又令輿入東宮，皇太子引上殿，親拜之。

translations.literal: He also ordered the chair into the Eastern Palace; the Heir Apparent led him up to the hall and bowed to him in person.
translations.idiomatic: He also had the chair brought into the Eastern Palace; the Heir Apparent led him up to the hall and bowed to him in person.

sentences.zh: 綱於是陳君臣父子之道、問寢視膳之方，理順辭直，聽者忘倦。

translations.literal: Gang thereupon set forth the Way of ruler and minister, father and son, and the methods of inquiring after health and attending to meals; his reasoning was orderly and his words straight, and listeners forgot weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Gang thereupon expounded the way of ruler and minister and of father and son, and the methods of inquiring after one's health and attending to meals; his reasoning was orderly and his words forthright, and those who heard him forgot weariness.

sentences.zh: 太子每親政事，太宗必令綱及左僕射房玄齡、侍中王珪侍坐。

translations.literal: Whenever the Heir Apparent personally handled government affairs, Taizong invariably had Gang together with the Left Director Fang Xuanling and the Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Gui sit in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Heir Apparent personally attended to government affairs, Taizong always had Gang sit with the Left Director Fang Xuanling and the Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Gui.

sentences.zh: 太子嘗商略古來君臣名教竭忠盡節之事，綱凜然曰：「托六尺之孤，寄百里之命，古人以為難，綱以為易。」

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent once discussed ancient affairs of ruler-minister teaching and exhausting loyalty to the utmost; Gang said sternly: "Entrusting a six-foot orphan and committing the fate of a hundred miles—men of old thought that hard; Gang thinks it easy."
translations.idiomatic: The Heir Apparent once discussed ancient affairs of moral teaching between ruler and minister and of exhausting loyalty to the utmost; Gang said sternly: "To entrust a six-foot orphan and commit the fate of a hundred miles—men of old thought that hard; I think it easy."

sentences.zh: 每吐論發言，皆辭色慷慨，有不可奪之志。

translations.literal: Each time he spoke his arguments, his tone and expression were ardent, with a will that could not be overborne.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he spoke, his tone and expression were ardent, with a resolve that could not be shaken.

sentences.zh: 及遇疾，太宗遣尚書左僕射房玄齡詣宅存問，賜絹二百匹。

translations.literal: When he fell ill, Taizong sent the Left Director Fang Xuanling to his house to inquire after him and bestowed two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill, Taizong sent the Left Director Fang Xuanling to his residence to inquire after him and bestowed two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 五年卒，年八十五。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died, aged eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he died, at the age of eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈開府儀同三司，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Ribbon of the First Rank; his posthumous title was Zhen (Upright).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Ribbon of the First Rank, with the posthumous title Zhen (Upright).

sentences.zh: 太子為之立碑。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent had a stele erected for him.
translations.idiomatic: The Heir Apparent had a stele erected for him.

sentences.zh: 初，周齊王憲女孀居孑立，綱自以齊王故吏，贍恤甚厚。

translations.literal: Earlier, a daughter of the Zhou Prince of Qi Xian lived as a widow alone; Gang, considering himself a former subordinate of the Prince of Qi, supported and comforted her generously.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, a daughter of the Northern Zhou Prince of Qi Xian lived as a widow in isolation; Gang, considering himself a former officer of the Prince of Qi, supported and comforted her generously.

sentences.zh: 及綱卒，其女被髮號哭，如喪所生焉。

translations.literal: When Gang died, the daughter let down her hair and wailed, as at the loss of a parent.
translations.idiomatic: When Gang died, the daughter let down her hair and wailed as though she had lost a parent.

sentences.zh: 孫少植子少植，隋武陽郡同功書佐，先綱卒。

translations.literal: His grandson Sun Shaozhi—Shaozhi, a tonggong clerical aide in Wuyang commandery under the Sui—died before Gang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Sun Shaozhi, a tonggong clerical aide in Wuyang commandery under the Sui, predeceased Gang.

sentences.zh: 少植子安仁，永徽中為太子左庶子。

translations.literal: Shaozhi's son Anren, in the Yonghui era served as Left Assistant Censor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozhi's son Anren served as Left Assistant Censor to the Heir Apparent during the Yonghui era.

sentences.zh: 屬太子被廢，歸於陳邸，宮僚皆逃散，無敢辭送者，安仁獨涕泣拜辭而去，朝野義之。

translations.literal: When the Heir Apparent was deposed and returned to Prince of Chen's mansion, palace staff all fled and none dared formally take leave; only Anren wept, bowed, and departed—court and country praised his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When the Heir Apparent was deposed and returned to the Prince of Chen's residence, the palace staff all fled and none dared formally take leave; only Anren wept, bowed in farewell, and departed—court and country praised his conduct.

sentences.zh: 後卒於恆州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he died as prefect of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later died while serving as prefect of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 鄭善果鄭善果，鄭州滎澤人也。

translations.literal: Zheng Shanguo—Zheng Shanguo was a native of Yingze in Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Shanguo came from Yingze in Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖孝穆，西魏少司空、岐州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xiaomu was Vice Minister of Works under Western Wei and prefect of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xiaomu had been Vice Minister of Works under Western Wei and prefect of Qi.

sentences.zh: 父誠，周大將軍、開封縣公。

translations.literal: His father Cheng was a great general of Zhou and Duke of Kaifeng county.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cheng had been a great general of Northern Zhou and Duke of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 大象初，討尉遲迥，力戰遇害。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Daxiang era, campaigning against Yuwen Jiong, he fought fiercely and met his death in battle.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Daxiang era, while campaigning against Yuwen Jiong, he fought fiercely and was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 善果年九歲，以父死王事，詔令襲其官爵。

translations.literal: Shanguo was nine years old; because his father died in the king's service, an edict ordered him to inherit his father's office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Shanguo was nine years old; because his father had died in the state's service, an edict ordered him to inherit his father's office and rank.

sentences.zh: 家人以其嬰孺，弗之告也，受冊悲慟，擗踴不能勝，觀者莫不為之流涕。

translations.literal: His family, because he was an infant, did not tell him; when he received the patent he grieved and stamped his feet in mourning beyond bearing, and none who watched failed to weep for him.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was still a child, his family had not told him; when he received the patent of succession he grieved and stamped his feet in mourning beyond bearing, and all who watched wept for him.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，改封武德郡公，拜沂州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Sui Kaihuang, his fief was changed to Duke of Wude commandery and he was appointed prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Sui Kaihuang his fief was changed to Duke of Wude commandery and he was appointed prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 大業中，累轉魯郡太守。

translations.literal: During Daye he was repeatedly transferred and became prefect of Lu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era he rose through successive posts to become prefect of Lu commandery.

sentences.zh: 善果篤慎，事親至孝。

translations.literal: Shanguo was sincere and cautious and served his parents with utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Shanguo was sincere and cautious and served his parents with the utmost filial piety.

sentences.zh: 母崔氏，賢明曉於政道，每善果理務，崔氏嘗於閣內聽之。

translations.literal: His mother, née Cui, was worthy and enlightened and understood governance; whenever Shanguo handled affairs, Lady Cui would listen from within the pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, of the Cui clan, was worthy and enlightened and understood governance; whenever Shanguo handled official business, Lady Cui would listen from within the pavilion.

sentences.zh: 聞其剖斷合理，歸則大悅；

translations.literal: if she heard his judgments were reasonable, on his return she was greatly pleased;
translations.idiomatic: if she heard that his judgments were sound, she was greatly pleased when he returned;

sentences.zh: 若處事不允，母則不與之言，善果伏於床前，終日不敢食。

translations.literal: if his handling of affairs was not fair, his mother would not speak with him; Shanguo would prostrate himself before her bed and for a whole day dared not eat.
translations.idiomatic: if his handling of affairs was unjust, his mother would not speak with him; Shanguo would prostrate himself before her bed and go the whole day without eating.

sentences.zh: 崔氏謂之曰：「吾非怒汝，反愧汝家耳。

translations.literal: Lady Cui said to him: "I am not angry with you—I am ashamed for your family.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cui said to him: "I am not angry with you—I am ashamed for your family.

sentences.zh: 汝先君在官清恪，未嘗問私，以身徇國，繼之以死。

translations.literal: Your late father in office was pure and scrupulous and never pursued private gain; he gave his body for the state and followed with his death.
translations.idiomatic: Your late father in office was pure and scrupulous and never pursued private gain; he gave his life for the state and followed that devotion with his death.

sentences.zh: 吾亦望汝繼父之心。

translations.literal: I also hope you will continue your father's heart.
translations.idiomatic: I also hope you will carry on your father's spirit.

sentences.zh: 自童子承襲茅土，今位至方伯，豈汝身能致之耶？

translations.literal: From childhood you inherited a fief; today you stand as a regional lord—could you have brought that about by yourself?
translations.idiomatic: From childhood you inherited a fief; today you stand as a regional lord—could you have brought that about by yourself?

sentences.zh: 安可不思此事而妄加嗔怒？

translations.literal: How can you fail to reflect on this and rashly give way to anger?
translations.idiomatic: How can you fail to reflect on this and rashly give way to anger?

sentences.zh: 內則墜爾家風，或亡官爵；

translations.literal: inwardly you would bring down your family's reputation and perhaps lose office and rank;
translations.idiomatic: inwardly you would bring down your family's reputation and perhaps lose office and rank;

sentences.zh: 外則虧天子之法，以取罪戾。

translations.literal: outwardly you would violate the Son of Heaven's laws and incur guilt.
translations.idiomatic: outwardly you would violate the Son of Heaven's laws and incur punishment.

sentences.zh: 吾寡婦也，有慈無威，使汝不知教訓，以負清忠之業，吾死之日，亦何面以事汝先君乎！」

translations.literal: I am a widow with kindness but no authority, and if I let you go without instruction and fail the work of purity and loyalty, on the day I die what face shall I have to serve your late father!"
translations.idiomatic: I am a widow with kindness but no authority; if I let you go without instruction and fail the work of purity and loyalty, on the day I die what face shall I have to meet your late father!"

sentences.zh: 善果由此遂勵己為清吏，所在有政績，百姓懷之。

translations.literal: From this Shanguo strove to make himself an upright official; wherever he served he had administrative achievements, and the people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: From this Shanguo strove to make himself an upright official; wherever he served he achieved good administration, and the people cherished him.

sentences.zh: 及朝京師，煬帝以其居官儉約，蒞政嚴明，與武威太守樊子蓋者為天下第一，各賞物千段，黃金百兩，再遷大理卿。

translations.literal: When he came to court at the capital, Emperor Yang, because his conduct in office was frugal and his governance strict and clear, ranked him with Fan Zigai, prefect of Wuwei, as first under heaven; each was rewarded with a thousand lengths of goods and a hundred taels of gold, and he was again promoted to Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to court, Emperor Yang ranked him with Fan Zigai, prefect of Wuwei, as the finest administrators in the realm for his frugal conduct in office and strict, clear governance; each was rewarded with a thousand lengths of goods and a hundred taels of gold, and Shanguo was again promoted to Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 後突厥圍煬帝於雁門，以守禦功，拜右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Later, when the Turks besieged Emperor Yang at Yanmen, for his merit in defense he was appointed Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Turks besieged Emperor Yang at Yanmen, he was appointed Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness for his merit in defense.

sentences.zh: 從幸江都。

translations.literal: He accompanied the emperor to Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor to Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及弒逆，署為民部尚書，隨化及至遼城。

translations.literal: Yuwen Huaji committed regicide and appointed him Minister of the Household; he followed Huaji to Liaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Huaji committed regicide, he appointed Shanguo Minister of the Household; Shanguo followed Huaji to Liaocheng.

sentences.zh: 淮安王神通圍化及，善果為化及守禦督戰，為流矢所中。

translations.literal: Prince of Huai'an Li Shentong besieged Huaji; Shanguo directed the defense and battle on Huaji's behalf and was struck by a stray arrow.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Huai'an Li Shentong besieged Huaji, Shanguo directed the defense on Huaji's behalf and was struck by a stray arrow.

sentences.zh: 及神通退還，竇建德進軍克之。

translations.literal: When Shentong withdrew, Dou Jiande advanced his army and took the place.
translations.idiomatic: When Shentong withdrew, Dou Jiande advanced and captured the place.

sentences.zh: 建德將王琮獲善果，誚之曰：「公隋室大臣也，自尊夫人亡後而清稱益衰，又忠臣子，奈何為弒君之賊殉命苦戰而傷痍若此？」

translations.literal: Jiande's general Wang Cong captured Shanguo and mocked him, saying: "You are a great minister of the Sui house; since your honored mother's death your reputation for purity has only declined; moreover you are a loyal minister's son—why do you die in bitter battle for a regicide and suffer wounds like these?"
translations.idiomatic: Jiande's general Wang Cong captured Shanguo and mocked him: "You are a great minister of the Sui; since your mother's death your reputation for purity has only declined; moreover you are a loyal minister's son—why do you fight to the death for a regicide and suffer wounds like these?"

sentences.zh: 善果深愧赧，欲自殺，偽中書令宋正本馳往救止之。

translations.literal: Shanguo was deeply ashamed and wished to kill himself; the false Director of the Secretariat Song Zhengben galloped to save and stop him.
translations.idiomatic: Shanguo was deeply ashamed and wished to kill himself; the false Director of the Secretariat Song Zhengben galloped to him and stopped him.

sentences.zh: 建德又不為之禮，乃奔相州。

translations.literal: Jiande also did not treat him with courtesy, so he fled to Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande also did not treat him with courtesy, so he fled to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 淮安王神通送於京師，高祖遇之甚厚，拜太子左庶子，檢校內史侍郎，封滎陽郡公。

translations.literal: Prince of Huai'an Shentong sent him to the capital; Gaozu received him very generously, appointed him Left Assistant Censor to the Heir Apparent and acting Vice Director of the Secretariat, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Xingyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Huai'an Shentong sent him to the capital; Gaozu received him very generously, appointed him Left Assistant Censor to the Heir Apparent and acting Vice Director of the Secretariat, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Xingyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 善果在東宮，數進忠言，多所匡諫。

translations.literal: Shanguo in the Eastern Palace repeatedly offered loyal words and remonstrated on many matters.
translations.idiomatic: In the Eastern Palace Shanguo repeatedly offered loyal counsel and remonstrated on many matters.

sentences.zh: 未幾，檢校大理卿，兼民部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he was acting Director of the Court of Judicial Review and concurrently Minister of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made acting Director of the Court of Judicial Review and concurrently Minister of the Household.

sentences.zh: 正身奉法，甚有善績。

translations.literal: He rectified his person and upheld the law and had very good achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He kept his person upright, upheld the law, and achieved excellent results.

sentences.zh: 制與裴寂等十人，每奏事及侍立，並令升殿，與從兄元璹在其數，時以為榮。

translations.literal: An ordinance grouped him with Pei Ji and nine others: whenever they presented matters or stood in attendance, all were ordered to ascend the hall; his cousin Yuan Ku was among the number, and at the time this was considered an honor.
translations.idiomatic: By ordinance he was grouped with Pei Ji and nine others: whenever they presented matters or stood in attendance, all were ordered to ascend the hall; his cousin Yuan Ku was among them, and at the time this was considered a great honor.

sentences.zh: 尋坐事免。

translations.literal: Before long he was dismissed on account of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was dismissed on account of an offense.

sentences.zh: 及山東平，持節為招撫大使，坐選舉不平除名。

translations.literal: When Shandong was pacified, bearing the staff of authority he served as commissioner for pacification; on account of unfair selections he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Shandong was pacified, he served as pacification commissioner bearing the staff of authority; on account of unfair selections he was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 後歷禮部、刑部二尚書。

translations.literal: Later he successively held the ministries of Rites and Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He later served successively as Minister of Rites and Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，出為岐州刺史，復以公事免。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan he went out as prefect of Qizhou and was again dismissed on account of public business.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenguan he was sent out as prefect of Qizhou and was again dismissed on account of official business.

sentences.zh: 三年，起為江州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year he was recalled as prefect of Jiangzhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was recalled as prefect of Jiangzhou and died in office.

sentences.zh: 從兄元璹元璹，隋岐州刺史、沛國公譯子也。

translations.literal: His cousin Yuan Ku—Yuan Ku was son of Yi, Sui prefect of Qi and Duke of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Yuan Ku was the son of Yi, who had been Sui prefect of Qi and Duke of Pei.

sentences.zh: 少以父功拜儀同大將軍，襲爵沛國公，累轉右武候將軍，改封莘國公。

translations.literal: In youth, on account of his father's merit, he was appointed General of the Palace with Equal Honours; he inherited the rank of Duke of Pei, was repeatedly transferred to General of the Right Martial Guards, and his fief was changed to Duke of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: In youth, on account of his father's merit, he was appointed General of the Palace with Equal Honours; he inherited the rank of Duke of Pei, rose through posts to General of the Right Martial Guards, and his fief was changed to Duke of Shen.

sentences.zh: 大業中，出為文城郡守。

translations.literal: During Daye he went out as prefect of Wencheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era he was sent out as prefect of Wencheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 義師至河東，元璹以郡來降，征拜太常卿。

translations.literal: When the righteous army reached Hedong, Yuan Ku surrendered the commandery and was summoned as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army reached Hedong, Yuan Ku surrendered the commandery and was summoned as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 及定京城，以本官兼參旗將軍。

translations.literal: When the capital was secured, he retained his post and concurrently served as General of the Banner of Participation.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was secured, he retained his post and concurrently served as General of the Banner of Participation.

sentences.zh: 元璹少在戎旅，尤明軍法，高祖常令巡諸軍，教其兵事。

translations.literal: Yuan Ku from youth had been in the army and was especially versed in military law; Gaozu often ordered him to tour the armies and teach them military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ku had been in the army from youth and was especially versed in military law; Gaozu often ordered him to tour the armies and instruct them in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 突厥始畢可汗弟乙力設代其兄為叱羅可汗，又劉武周將宋金剛與叱羅共為掎角，來寇汾、晉。

translations.literal: The younger brother of the Turkic Shibi Qaghan, Yilish, replaced his brother as Chiluo Qaghan; moreover Liu Wuzhou's general Song Jingang and Chiluo acted as pincers and came to raid Fen and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Yilish, younger brother of the Turkic Shibi Qaghan, replaced his brother as Chiluo Qaghan; moreover Liu Wuzhou's general Song Jingang and Chiluo coordinated as pincers and raided Fen and Jin.

sentences.zh: 詔元璹入蕃，諭以禍福，叱羅竟不納，乃欲總其部落，入寇太原，以為武周聲援。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yuan Ku to enter the barbarian lands and instruct Chiluo on fortune and misfortune; Chiluo in the end did not accept, and wished instead to gather his tribes and invade Taiyuan as a sounding support for Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Yuan Ku into the steppe to instruct Chiluo on fortune and misfortune; Chiluo would not accept and instead wished to gather his tribes, invade Taiyuan, and support Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，叱羅遇疾，療之弗愈，其下疑元璹令人毒之，乃囚執元璹，不得歸，叱羅竟死。

translations.literal: Before long Chiluo fell ill and treatment did not cure him; his subordinates suspected Yuan Ku of having had him poisoned, imprisoned Yuan Ku, and he could not return; Chiluo in the end died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Chiluo fell ill and could not be cured; his followers suspected Yuan Ku of having had him poisoned, imprisoned Yuan Ku so he could not return, and Chiluo eventually died.

sentences.zh: 頡利嗣立，留元璹，每隨其牙帳，經數年。

translations.literal: Jieli succeeded to the throne, kept Yuan Ku, and each day he followed the royal tent—for several years.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli succeeded to the throne, kept Yuan Ku with him, and he followed the royal tent for several years.

sentences.zh: 頡利後聞高祖遺其財物，又許結婚，始放元璹來還。

translations.literal: Later Jieli heard that Gaozu had sent him goods and also promised a marriage alliance, and only then released Yuan Ku to return.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jieli heard that Gaozu had sent him goods and also promised a marriage alliance, and only then released Yuan Ku to return.

sentences.zh: 高祖勞之曰：「卿在虜庭，累載拘繫，蘇武弗之過也。」

translations.literal: Gaozu comforted him, saying: "You were in the barbarian court, detained for many years—Su Wu did no more."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu comforted him: "You were in the barbarian court, detained for many years—even Su Wu did no more."

sentences.zh: 拜鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Court for Dependencies.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director of the Court for Dependencies.

sentences.zh: 尋而突厥又寇并州，時元璹在母喪，高祖令墨絰充使招慰。

translations.literal: Before long the Turks again raided Bingzhou; at the time Yuan Ku was in mourning for his mother, but Gaozu ordered him to wear unhemmed mourning garb and serve as envoy to summon and comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Turks again raided Bingzhou; Yuan Ku was then in mourning for his mother, but Gaozu ordered him to wear unhemmed mourning garb and serve as envoy to summon and comfort them.

sentences.zh: 突厥從介休至晉州，數百里間，精騎數十萬，填映山谷。

translations.literal: The Turks from Jiexiu to Jinzhou—for several hundred li, elite horsemen in the hundreds of thousands filled and covered the valleys.
translations.idiomatic: From Jiexiu to Jinzhou the Turks stretched for several hundred li, with hundreds of thousands of elite horsemen filling the valleys.

sentences.zh: 及見元璹，責中國違背之事，元璹隨機應對，竟無所屈，因數突厥背誕之罪，突厥大慚，不能報。

translations.literal: When they saw Yuan Ku, they reproached China for breaches of faith; Yuan Ku answered as occasion demanded and in the end was not overborne; he then enumerated the Turks' crimes of faithlessness, and the Turks were greatly ashamed and could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: When they saw Yuan Ku, they reproached China for breaches of faith; Yuan Ku answered as the occasion required and was not overborne; he then enumerated the Turks' crimes of faithlessness, and the Turks were greatly ashamed and could not reply.

sentences.zh: 元璹又謂頡利曰：「漢與突厥，風俗各異，漢得突厥，既不能臣，突厥得漢，復何所用？

translations.literal: Yuan Ku also said to Jieli: "Han and the Turks differ in customs; if Han obtains Turks, they cannot be made subjects; if Turks obtain Han, of what use are they?
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ku also said to Jieli: "Han and the Turks differ in customs; if the Han obtain Turks, they cannot be made subjects; if the Turks obtain Han subjects, of what use are they?

sentences.zh: 且抄掠資財，皆入將士，在於可汗，一無所得。

translations.literal: Moreover the goods seized in raids all go to officers and soldiers; as for the qaghan, he gains nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the goods seized in raids all go to officers and soldiers; as for the qaghan, he gains nothing.

sentences.zh: 不如早收兵馬，遣使和好，國家必有重賚，幣帛皆入可汗，免為劬勞，坐受利益。

translations.literal: Better to withdraw the troops and horses early, send envoys to make peace—the state will surely give rich rewards, and silk and cloth will all enter the qaghan's hands; you are spared toil and receive benefit while seated.
translations.idiomatic: Better to withdraw your troops early, send envoys to make peace—the state will surely give rich rewards, and silk and cloth will all go to the qaghan; you are spared toil and receive benefit while seated.

sentences.zh: 大唐初有天下，即與可汗結為兄弟，行人往來，音問不絕。

translations.literal: When Great Tang first possessed the realm, it at once bound brotherhood with the qaghan; travelers went back and forth and messages never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When Great Tang first possessed the realm, it at once entered brotherhood with the qaghan; envoys went back and forth and messages never ceased.

sentences.zh: 今乃舍善取怨，違多就少，何也？」

translations.literal: Now you abandon the good and take up resentment, go against the many for the few—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Now you abandon what is good and take up resentment, go against the many for the few—why?"

sentences.zh: 頡利納其言，即引還。

translations.literal: Jieli accepted his words and at once led his forces back.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli accepted his words and at once led his forces back.

sentences.zh: 太宗致書慰之曰：「知公已共可汗結和，遂使邊亭息警，爟火不然。

translations.literal: Taizong sent a letter comforting him: "Knowing that you have made peace with the qaghan, the border posts are thus quiet of alarms and beacon fires do not blaze.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent a letter of comfort: "Knowing that you have made peace with the qaghan, the border posts are quiet of alarms and the beacon fires do not blaze.

sentences.zh: 和戎之功，豈唯魏絳，金石之錫，固當非遠。」

translations.literal: The merit of pacifying the barbarians—is it only Wei Jiang's? Rewards of metal and stone surely cannot be far off."
translations.idiomatic: The merit of pacifying the barbarians—is it only Wei Jiang's? Rewards of metal and stone surely cannot be far off."

sentences.zh: 元璹自義寧已來，五入蕃充使，幾至於死者數矣。

translations.literal: From Yining onward Yuan Ku five times entered the barbarian lands as envoy and several times nearly died.
translations.idiomatic: From Yining onward Yuan Ku entered the steppe five times as envoy and several times nearly died.

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年，又使入突厥，還奏曰：「突厥興亡，唯以羊馬為準。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenguan he was again sent into the Turks; on his return he reported: "The rise and fall of the Turks depends solely on sheep and horses as the measure.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenguan he was again sent among the Turks; on his return he reported: "The rise and fall of the Turks depends solely on sheep and horses as the measure.

sentences.zh: 今六畜疲羸，人皆菜色，又其牙內炊飯，化而為血。

translations.literal: Now the six domestic animals are worn and weak, the people all have the hue of vegetables, and moreover within the royal tent cooked rice turned into blood.
translations.idiomatic: Now the livestock are worn and weak, the people all show the pallor of famine, and moreover within the royal tent cooked rice turned into blood.

sentences.zh: 征祥如此，不出三年，必當覆滅。」

translations.literal: Ominous signs such as these—within three years they will surely be overthrown."
translations.idiomatic: With omens such as these, within three years they will surely be destroyed."

sentences.zh: 太宗然之。

translations.literal: Taizong agreed with this.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong agreed with this.

sentences.zh: 無幾，突厥果敗。

translations.literal: Before long the Turks were indeed defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Turks were indeed defeated.

sentences.zh: 元璹後累轉左武候大將軍，坐事免。

translations.literal: Later Yuan Ku was repeatedly transferred to General of the Left Martial Guards and was dismissed on account of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yuan Ku rose to General of the Left Martial Guards and was dismissed on account of an offense.

sentences.zh: 尋起為宜州刺史，復封沛國公。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled as prefect of Yizhou and again enfeoffed as Duke of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled as prefect of Yizhou and again enfeoffed as Duke of Pei.

sentences.zh: 元璹有干略，所在頗著聲譽。

translations.literal: Yuan Ku had capacity and strategy; wherever he served he won considerable reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ku had capacity and strategic talent; wherever he served he won a considerable reputation.

sentences.zh: 然其父譯事繼母失溫凊之禮，隋文帝曾賜以《孝經》；

translations.literal: Yet his father Yi in serving his stepmother failed the rites of warmth in winter and coolness in summer; Emperor Wen of Sui once bestowed on him the Classic of Filial Piety;
translations.idiomatic: Yet his father Yi in serving his stepmother failed the rites of warmth in winter and coolness in summer; Emperor Wen of Sui once bestowed on him the Classic of Filial Piety;

sentences.zh: 至元璹事親，又不以孝聞，清論鄙之。

translations.literal: as for Yuan Ku in serving his parents, he likewise was not known for filial piety, and pure opinion despised him.
translations.idiomatic: as for Yuan Ku in serving his parents, he likewise was not known for filial piety, and respectable opinion despised him.

sentences.zh: 二十年卒，贈幽州刺史，謚曰簡。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he died; he was posthumously made prefect of Youzhou, with posthumous title Jian (Simple).
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he died; he was posthumously made prefect of Youzhou, with the posthumous title Jian (Simple).

sentences.zh: 弟孫杲知名，則天時為天官侍郎。

translations.literal: His younger brother's grandson Sun Gao was well known; in the time of Empress Zetian he was Vice Director of the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother's grandson Sun Gao was well known; under Empress Wu he served as Vice Director of the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 楊恭仁楊恭仁，本名綸，弘農華陰人，隋司空、觀王雄之長子也。

translations.literal: Yang Gongren—Yang Gongren, original name Lun, was a native of Huayin in Hongnong, eldest son of Xiong, Sui Minister of Works and Prince of Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gongren, originally named Lun, came from Huayin in Hongnong; he was the eldest son of Xiong, Sui Minister of Works and Prince of Guan.

sentences.zh: 隋仁壽中，累除甘州刺史。

translations.literal: During Sui Renshou he was repeatedly transferred and removed as prefect of Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Sui Renshou era he rose through successive appointments to prefect of Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 恭仁務舉大綱，不為苛察，戎夏安之。

translations.literal: Gongren devoted himself to the great outlines and did not engage in harsh scrutiny; barbarians and Chinese were at peace under him.
translations.idiomatic: Gongren devoted himself to the great outlines of governance and did not engage in harsh scrutiny; both barbarians and Chinese were at peace under him.

sentences.zh: 文帝謂雄曰：「恭仁在州，甚有善政，非唯朕舉得人，亦是卿義方所致也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen said to Xiong: "Gongren in the prefecture has very good administration—not only did I choose the right man, it is also due to your righteous instruction."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen said to Xiong: "Gongren in the prefecture has governed very well—not only did I choose the right man, it is also due to your righteous instruction."

sentences.zh: 大業初，轉吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Daye era he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 楊玄感作亂，煬帝制恭仁率兵經略，與玄感戰於破陵，大敗之。

translations.literal: Yang Xuangan rebelled; Emperor Yang ordered Gongren to lead troops in campaign, fought Xuangan at Poling, and defeated him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, Emperor Yang ordered Gongren to lead troops against him; Gongren fought Xuangan at Poling and defeated him utterly.

sentences.zh: 玄感兄弟挺身遁走，恭仁與屈突通等追討獲之。

translations.literal: Xuangan's brothers straightened their bodies and fled; Gongren with Qu Tutong and others pursued in reprisal and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan's brothers broke away and fled; Gongren, together with Qu Tutong and others, gave chase and captured them.

sentences.zh: 軍旋，煬帝召入內殿，謂曰：「我聞破陵之陣，唯卿力戰，功最難比。

translations.literal: The army returned; Emperor Yang summoned him into the inner hall and addressed him, saying: "I heard that at the Poling battle-array you alone fought with full force, and your merit is hardest to compare.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, Emperor Yang summoned him into the inner hall and said: "I have heard that at Poling you alone fought with all your strength, and your achievement is beyond comparison.

sentences.zh: 雖知卿奉法清慎，都不知勇決如此也。」

translations.literal: Although I knew you uphold the law with clarity and caution, I never knew you were so bold and decisive."
translations.idiomatic: Though I knew you upheld the law with clarity and caution, I never knew you were so bold and decisive."

sentences.zh: 納言蘇威曰：「仁者必有勇，固非虛也。」

translations.literal: Chancellor Su Wei said: "The benevolent man must have courage—this is truly no empty saying."
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Su Wei said: "The benevolent man must have courage—this is by no means an empty maxim."

sentences.zh: 時蘇威及左衛大將軍宇文述、御史大夫裴蘊、黃門侍郎裴矩等皆受詔參掌選事，多納賄賂，士流嗟怨。

translations.literal: At that time Su Wei, Left Guard General-in-Chief Yuwen Shu, Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun, Huangmen Attendant-in-Ordinary Pei Ju, and others had all received edicts to participate in managing selection affairs; they accepted many bribes, and men of standing sighed in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Su Wei, Left Guard General-in-Chief Yuwen Shu, Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun, Huangmen Attendant-in-Ordinary Pei Ju, and others had all received edicts to help manage selection affairs; they took many bribes, and men of standing sighed in resentment.

sentences.zh: 恭仁獨雅正自守，不為蘊等所容，由是出為河南道大使，討捕盜賊。

translations.literal: Gongren alone maintained elegant rectitude and self-restraint and was not tolerated by Yun and the others; on this account he was sent out as envoy of the Henan Circuit to hunt down bandits and thieves.
translations.idiomatic: Gongren alone maintained elegant rectitude and would not be tolerated by Yun and the others; on this account he was sent out as envoy of the Henan Circuit to hunt down bandits and thieves.

sentences.zh: 時天下大亂，行至譙郡，為硃粲所敗，奔還江都。

translations.literal: At that time the realm was in great disorder; when he reached Qiao commandery he was defeated by Zhu Can and fled back to Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the realm was in great disorder; when he reached Qiao commandery he was defeated by Zhu Can and fled back to Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及弒逆，署吏部尚書，隨至河北，為化及守魏縣。

translations.literal: Yuwen Huaji committed regicide and appointed him Minister of Personnel; following to Hebei, he had Gongren defend Wei county for Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Huaji committed regicide, he appointed Gongren Minister of Personnel; following Huaji to Hebei, Gongren was left to defend Wei county for him.

sentences.zh: 時元寶藏據有魏郡，會行人魏徵說下寶藏，執恭仁送於京師。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Baocang held Weijun; it happened that the envoy Wei Zheng persuaded Baocang to submit, and he seized Gongren and sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuan Baocang held Weijun; the envoy Wei Zheng persuaded Baocang to submit, and Baocang seized Gongren and sent him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 高祖甚禮遇之，拜黃門侍郎，封觀國公。

translations.literal: Gaozu treated him with great courtesy, appointing him Huangmen Attendant-in-Ordinary and enfeoffing him as Duke of Guan State.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu treated him with great courtesy, appointing him Huangmen Attendant-in-Ordinary and enfeoffing him as Duke of Guan State.

sentences.zh: 尋為涼州總管。

translations.literal: Before long he became Commander of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he became Commander of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 恭仁素習邊事，深悉羌胡情偽，推心馭下，人吏悅服，自蔥嶺已東，併入朝貢。

translations.literal: Gongren had long been versed in frontier affairs and thoroughly understood the true and false among the Qiang and Hu; he won men's hearts in governing subordinates, and officials and clerks were pleased and submitted—from beyond the Onion Mountains eastward, all entered the court as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Gongren had long been versed in frontier affairs and thoroughly understood the true and false among the Qiang and Hu; he won the hearts of those below him, and officials and clerks were pleased to submit—from beyond the Onion Mountains eastward, all came to court bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遙授納言，總管如故。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed in absentia as Chancellor, while remaining Commander as before.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed in absentia as Chancellor, while remaining Commander as before.

sentences.zh: 俄而突厥頡利可汗率眾數萬奄至州境，恭仁隨方備御，多設疑兵，頡利懼而退走。

translations.literal: Soon the Tujue qaghan Illig led tens of thousands straight to the prefectural border; Gongren defended according to circumstances on every side and set up many decoy troops; Illig feared and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Tujue qaghan Illig led tens of thousands straight to the prefectural border; Gongren defended on every side as circumstances required and set up many decoy troops, and Illig withdrew in fear.

sentences.zh: 屬瓜州刺史賀拔威擁兵作亂，朝廷憚遠，未遑征討。

translations.literal: It happened that the prefect of Guazhou Heba Wei raised troops in rebellion; the court dreaded the distance and had no leisure to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the prefect of Guazhou Heba Wei raised troops in rebellion; the court dreaded the distance and had no leisure to campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 恭仁乃募驍勇，倍道兼進，賊不虞兵至之速，克其二城。

translations.literal: Gongren then recruited fierce warriors and doubled the pace day and night; the rebels did not anticipate the army's arriving so swiftly and took two of their cities.
translations.idiomatic: Gongren then recruited fierce warriors and pressed forward at double speed; the rebels did not expect the army to arrive so swiftly, and he captured two of their cities.

sentences.zh: 恭仁悉放俘虜，賊眾感其寬惠，遂相率執威而降。

translations.literal: Gongren entirely released the captives; the rebel host was moved by his leniency and favor, and successively seized Wei and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Gongren released all the captives; the rebel host was moved by his leniency, and they successively seized Wei and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 久之，征拜吏部尚書，遷左衛大將軍、鼓旗將軍。

translations.literal: After a long while he was summoned and appointed Minister of Personnel, transferred to Left Guard General-in-Chief and General of Drum and Banner.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was summoned and appointed Minister of Personnel, then transferred to Left Guard General-in-Chief and General of Drum and Banner.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，拜雍州牧，加左光祿大夫，行揚州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was appointed Prefect of Yongzhou, with added Left Glory Grand Master of the Palace, acting as Long Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou Grand Protectorate.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was appointed Prefect of Yongzhou, with the added title Left Glory Grand Master of the Palace, and served as acting Long Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou Grand Protectorate.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷洛州都督。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Protector-General of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to Protector-General of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「洛陽要重，古難其人。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Luoyang is strategically heavy; since antiquity it has been hard to find the right man.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Luoyang is strategically vital; since antiquity it has been hard to find the right man.

sentences.zh: 朕之子弟多矣，恐非所任，特以委公也。」

translations.literal: I have many sons and younger relatives, yet I fear none is fit for the post—I entrust it to you alone."
translations.idiomatic: I have many sons and younger kin, yet I fear none is fit for the duty—I entrust it to you alone."

sentences.zh: 恭仁性虛澹，必以禮度自居，謙恭下士，未嘗忤物，時人方之石慶。

translations.literal: Gongren by nature was unassuming and mild; he invariably held himself to ritual propriety, was modest and courteous to men below him, and never offended others; people of the time compared him to Shi Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Gongren was by nature unassuming and mild; he invariably held himself to ritual propriety, was modest and courteous to men below him, and never gave offense; people of the time compared him to Shi Qing.

sentences.zh: 恭仁弟師道，尚桂陽公主，從侄女為巢剌王妃，弟子思敬，尚安平公主，連姻帝室，益見崇重。

translations.literal: Gongren's younger brother Shidao married Princess Guiyang; his brother's daughter by marriage became consort of the Prince of Chao, and his son by marriage Sijing married Princess Ping'an—through marriage with the imperial house he came to be honored all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Gongren's younger brother Shidao married Princess Guiyang; his brother's daughter by marriage became consort of the Prince of Chao, and his son by marriage Sijing married Princess Ping'an—through marriage with the imperial house the family came to be honored all the more.

sentences.zh: 後以老病乞骸骨，聽以特進歸第。

translations.literal: Later, owing to old age and illness, he petitioned to retire on bones; he was permitted to return home with the special-advancement stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Later, owing to old age and illness, he petitioned to retire; he was permitted to return home with the special-advancement stipend.

sentences.zh: 十三年卒，冊贈開府儀同三司、潭州都督，陪葬昭陵，謚曰孝。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died; posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Mentor of the Palace with golden insignia and Protector-General of Tanzhou, buried with attendant honors at Zhaoling, posthumous name Xiao (Filial).
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he died; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Mentor of the Palace with golden insignia and Protector-General of Tanzhou, buried with attendant honors at Zhaoling, and given the posthumous name Xiao (Filial).

sentences.zh: 子思訓子思訓襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Sixun—Sixun inherited the peerage.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sixun inherited the peerage.

sentences.zh: 顯慶中，歷右屯衛將軍。

translations.literal: During Xianqing he served successively as General of the Right Garrison Guards.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianqing he served successively as General of the Right Garrison Guards.

sentences.zh: 時右衛大將軍慕容寶節有愛妾，置於別宅，嘗邀思訓就之宴樂。

translations.literal: At that time the Right Guard General-in-Chief Murong Baojie had a beloved concubine kept in a separate residence; he once invited Sixun there for feasting and revelry.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Right Guard General-in-Chief Murong Baojie had a beloved concubine kept in a separate residence; he once invited Sixun there for feasting and revelry.

sentences.zh: 思訓深責寶節與其妻隔絕，妾等怒，密以毒藥置酒，思訓飲盡便死。

translations.literal: Sixun sternly reproached Baojie for separating himself from his wife; the concubines grew angry and secretly placed poison in the wine—Sixun drank it all and died at once.
translations.idiomatic: Sixun sternly reproached Baojie for separating himself from his wife; the concubines grew angry and secretly placed poison in the wine—Sixun drank it all and died at once.

sentences.zh: 寶節坐是配嶺表。

translations.literal: Baojie on this account was banished to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Baojie on this account was banished to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 思訓妻又詣闕稱冤，制遣使就斬之。

translations.literal: Sixun's wife again went to the palace gates to plead her wrong; an edict dispatched envoys to go and execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Sixun's wife again went to the palace gates to plead her wrong; an edict dispatched envoys to go and execute Baojie.

sentences.zh: 仍改《賊盜律》，以毒藥殺人之科，更從重法。

translations.literal: The Theft and Robbery Statutes were still revised: the article on killing by poison was made subject to heavier penalties.
translations.idiomatic: The Theft and Robbery Statutes were also revised: the article on killing by poison was made subject to heavier penalties.

sentences.zh: 思訓孫睿交，本名璬，少襲爵觀國公，尚中宗女長寧公主。
