translations.literal: Sixun's grandson Ruijiao, original name Jiao, in youth inherited the peerage Duke of Guan State and married Princess Changning, daughter of Emperor Zhongzong.
translations.idiomatic: Sixun's grandson Ruijiao, originally named Jiao, inherited the peerage Duke of Guan State in his youth and married Princess Changning, daughter of Emperor Zhongzong.

sentences.zh: 預誅張易之有功，賜實封五百戶。

translations.literal: For merit in the preliminary execution of Zhang Yizhi he was granted five hundred households of substantive fief.
translations.idiomatic: For merit in the preliminary execution of Zhang Yizhi he was granted five hundred households of substantive fief.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，為秘書監。

translations.literal: During Shenlong he was Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: During Shenlong he was Director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 後被貶，卒於絳州別駕。

translations.literal: Later he was demoted and died while serving as Vice-Prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was demoted and died while serving as Vice-Prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 弟續恭仁弟續，頗有辭學。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xu—Gongren's younger brother Xu—was quite accomplished in literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xu—Gongren's younger brother Xu—was quite accomplished in literary learning.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，為鄆州刺史。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan he was Prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan he was Prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 續孫執柔，則天時為地官尚書，則天以外氏近屬，甚優寵之。

translations.literal: Xu's grandson Zhirou—during Wu Zetian's time he was Minister of the Ministry of Earth; because he was a close relative on her mother's side, she greatly favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu's grandson Zhirou—during Wu Zetian's time he was Minister of the Ministry of Earth; because he was a close relative on her mother's side, she greatly favored him.

sentences.zh: 時武承嗣、攸寧相次知政事，則天嘗曰：「我今當宗及外家，常一人為宰相。」

translations.literal: At that time Wu Chengsi and Youning succeeded one another in managing state affairs; Wu Zetian once said: "Hereafter in the clan and the maternal kin I shall always have one man as Chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wu Chengsi and Youning succeeded one another in managing state affairs; Wu Zetian once said: "Hereafter in the clan and the maternal kin I shall always have one man as Chancellor."

sentences.zh: 由是執柔同中書門下三品，尋卒。

translations.literal: On this account Zhirou became coequal with Secretariat-Chancellery of the Third Rank; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: On this account Zhirou became coequal with Secretariat-Chancellery of the Third Rank; before long he died.

sentences.zh: 執柔子滔，開元中官至吏部侍郎、同州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhirou's son Tao—in the Kaiyuan era reached the posts of Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Prefect of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhirou's son Tao—in the Kaiyuan era reached the posts of Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 執柔弟執一，神龍初，以誅張易之功封河東郡公，累至右金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Zhirou's younger brother Zhiyi—in the beginning of Shenlong, for merit in executing Zhang Yizhi was enfeoffed Duke of Hedong commandery, and rose successively to General-in-Chief of the Right Golden-Avenging Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Zhirou's younger brother Zhiyi—in the beginning of Shenlong, for merit in executing Zhang Yizhi was enfeoffed Duke of Hedong commandery, and rose successively to General-in-Chief of the Right Golden-Avenging Guards.

sentences.zh: 少弟師道恭仁少弟師道，隋末自洛陽歸國，授上儀同，為備身左右。

translations.literal: His youngest brother Shidao—Gongren's youngest brother Shidao, at the end of Sui returned to the Tang from Luoyang, was appointed Upper Pillar of State with golden insignia, and served as an attendant in the personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest brother Shidao—Gongren's youngest brother Shidao—at the end of Sui returned to the Tang from Luoyang, was appointed Upper Pillar of State with golden insignia, and served as an attendant in the personal guard.

sentences.zh: 尋尚桂陽公主，超拜吏部侍郎，累轉太常卿，封安德郡公。

translations.literal: Before long he married Princess Guiyang, was promoted over the regular order to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, rose through successive transfers to Minister of Rites, and was enfeoffed Duke of Ande commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he married Princess Guiyang, was promoted over the regular order to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, rose through successive transfers to Minister of Rites, and was enfeoffed Duke of Ande commandery.

sentences.zh: 貞觀七年，代魏徵為侍中。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhenguan he replaced Wei Zheng as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Zhenguan he replaced Wei Zheng as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 性周慎謹密，未嘗漏洩內事，親友或問禁中之言，乃更對以他語。

translations.literal: By nature he was thorough, cautious, and secretive; he never leaked inner-court affairs—if kin or friends asked about palace speech, he would answer with other topics instead.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was thorough, cautious, and secretive; he never leaked inner-court affairs—if kin or friends asked about palace matters, he would answer with other topics instead.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「吾少窺漢史，至孔光不言溫室之樹，每欽其餘風，所庶幾也。」

translations.literal: He once said: "In youth I glanced into Han histories; when I came to Kong Guang not speaking of the trees in the Greenhouse, I always admired that lingering virtue—it is what I hope in some measure to emulate."
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "In youth I glanced into Han histories; when I came to Kong Guang not speaking of the trees in the Greenhouse, I always admired that lingering virtue—it is what I hope in some measure to emulate."

sentences.zh: 師道退朝後，必引當時英俊，宴集園池，而文會之盛，當時莫比。

translations.literal: After Shidao left court he would always gather the outstanding men of the time for banquets in garden and pool; for the splendor of literary gatherings none of the day could compare.
translations.idiomatic: After Shidao left court he would always gather the outstanding men of the time for banquets in garden and pool; for the splendor of literary gatherings none of the day could compare.

sentences.zh: 雅善篇什，又工草隸，酣賞之際，援筆直書，有如宿構。

translations.literal: He was skilled in poetry and also adept at cursive and clerical script—amid his cups he would take up the brush and write straight off, as though composed long before.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in poetry and also adept at cursive and clerical script—amid his cups he would take up the brush and write straight off, as though composed long before.

sentences.zh: 太宗每見師道所制，必吟諷嗟賞之。

translations.literal: Whenever the Emperor saw what Shidao composed he would recite it and sigh in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Emperor saw what Shidao composed he would recite it and sigh in admiration.

sentences.zh: 十三年，轉中書令。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to Secretariat Director.

sentences.zh: 太子承乾逆謀事洩，與長孫無忌、房玄齡同按其獄。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Chenghan's treasonous plot leaked out, he together with Zhangsun Wuji and Fang Xuanling investigated the case.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Chenghan's treasonous plot leaked out, he together with Zhangsun Wuji and Fang Xuanling investigated the case.

sentences.zh: 師道妻前夫之子趙節與承乾通謀，師道微諷太宗，冀活之，由是獲譴，罷知機密。

translations.literal: Shidao's wife's son by a former marriage Zhao Jie had conspired with Chenghan; Shidao subtly urged the Emperor, hoping to save him—and on this account was reprimanded and dismissed from handling confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao's wife's son by a former marriage Zhao Jie had conspired with Chenghan; Shidao subtly urged the Emperor, hoping to save him—and on this account was reprimanded and dismissed from handling confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 轉吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 師道貴家子，四海人物，未能委練，所署用多非其才，而深抑貴勢及其親黨，以避嫌疑，時論譏之。

translations.literal: Shidao was a son of an eminent house; with all the personages under heaven he had not yet gained seasoned experience—those he appointed were often not fit for their posts, while he deeply repressed noble clans and their kin and associates to avoid suspicion; opinion of the time criticized him.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao was a son of an eminent house; with all the personages under heaven he had not yet gained seasoned experience—those he appointed were often not fit for their posts, while he deeply repressed noble clans and their kin and associates to avoid suspicion; opinion of the time criticized him.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗從容謂侍臣曰：「楊師道性行純善，自無愆過。

translations.literal: The Emperor once said at leisure to the attendant ministers: "Yang Shidao's conduct is purely good; he has no fault of his own.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once said at leisure to the attendant ministers: "Yang Shidao's conduct is purely good; he has no fault of his own.

sentences.zh: 而情實怯懦，未甚更事，緩急不可得力。」

translations.literal: Yet in truth he is timid and weak, not very experienced in affairs—in urgent need he cannot deliver force."
translations.idiomatic: Yet in truth he is timid and weak, not very experienced in affairs—in urgent need he cannot deliver force."

sentences.zh: 未幾，從征高麗，攝中書令。

translations.literal: Before long he followed the campaign against Koguryŏ as acting Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he followed the campaign against Koguryŏ as acting Secretariat Director.

sentences.zh: 及軍還，有毀之者，稍貶為工部尚書，尋轉太常卿。

translations.literal: When the army returned, there were those who slandered him; he was slightly demoted to Minister of Works, and soon transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, there were those who slandered him; he was slightly demoted to Minister of Works, and soon transferred to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 二十一年卒，贈吏部尚書、并州都督，陪葬昭陵，賜東園秘器，並為立碑。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he died; posthumously awarded Minister of Personnel and Protector-General of Bingzhou, buried with attendant honors at Zhaoling, granted eastern-garden secret vessels, and a stele was erected for him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he died; he was posthumously awarded Minister of Personnel and Protector-General of Bingzhou, buried with attendant honors at Zhaoling, granted eastern-garden secret vessels, and a stele was erected for him.

sentences.zh: 子豫之，尚巢剌王女壽春縣主。

translations.literal: His son Yuzhi married the daughter of the Prince of Chao, Princess of Shouchun county.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuzhi married the daughter of the Prince of Chao, Princess of Shouchun county.

sentences.zh: 居母喪，與永嘉公主淫亂，為主婿竇奉節所擒，具五刑而殺之。

translations.literal: While in mourning for his mother he committed debauchery with Princess Yongjia; he was seized by the princess's husband Dou Fengjie, and after full five punishments was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: While in mourning for his mother he committed debauchery with Princess Yongjia; he was seized by the princess's husband Dou Fengjie, and after the full five punishments was put to death.

sentences.zh: 師道兄子思玄，高宗時為吏部侍郎、國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Shidao's elder brother's son Sixuan—in Gaozong's time was Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Chancellor of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao's elder brother's son Sixuan—in Gaozong's time was Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Chancellor of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 玄弟思敬，禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Sixuan's younger brother Sijing was Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Sixuan's younger brother Sijing was Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 師道從兄子崇敬，太子詹事。

translations.literal: Shidao's cousin's son Chongjing was Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao's cousin's son Chongjing was Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 始恭仁父雄在隋，以同姓寵貴，自武德之後，恭仁兄弟名位尤盛，則天時，又以外戚崇寵。

translations.literal: In the beginning, Gongren's father Xiong under the Sui, because of sharing the surname, received favor and dignity; after Wude, the Gongren brothers' names and posts were especially prominent; in Wu Zetian's time they were again exalted as maternal kin.
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning, Gongren's father Xiong under the Sui, because of sharing the imperial surname, received favor and dignity; after Wude, the Gongren brothers' names and posts were especially prominent; in Wu Zetian's time they were again exalted as maternal kin.

sentences.zh: 一家之內，駙馬三人，王妃五人，贈皇后一人，三品已上官二十餘人，遂為盛族。

translations.literal: Within one household there were three imperial sons-in-law, five princesses-consort, one posthumously honored empress, and more than twenty officials of the third rank and above—they thus became a great clan.
translations.idiomatic: Within one household there were three imperial sons-in-law, five princesses-consort, one posthumously honored empress, and more than twenty officials of the third rank and above—they thus became a great clan.

sentences.zh: 皇甫無逸皇甫無逸，字仁儉，安定烏氏人。

translations.literal: Huangfu Wuyi—Huangfu Wuyi, styled Renjian, was a native of Wushi in Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Wuyi, styled Renjian, came from Wushi in Anding.

sentences.zh: 父誕，隋并州總管府司馬。

translations.literal: His father Dan was Sui Prefectural Army Aide-de-Camp of Bingzhou General Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dan had served as Prefectural Army Aide-de-Camp of the Bingzhou General Headquarters under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 其先安定著姓，徙居京兆萬年。

translations.literal: His ancestors were a renowned surname of Anding and migrated to settle in Wannian, Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors were a renowned clan of Anding and had migrated to settle in Wannian, Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 仁壽末，漢王諒於并州起兵反，誕抗節不從，為諒所殺。

translations.literal: At the end of Renshou, the Prince of Han Liang raised troops in rebellion at Bingzhou; Dan resisted and would not follow, and Liang killed him.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Renshou, the Prince of Han Liang raised troops in rebellion at Bingzhou; Dan resisted and would not follow, and Liang killed him.

sentences.zh: 無逸時在長安，聞諒反，即同居喪之禮。

translations.literal: Wuyi was then in Chang'an; when he heard Liang had rebelled he immediately observed the mourning rites for one dwelling together.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi was then in Chang'an; when he heard Liang had rebelled he immediately observed the mourning rites for one dwelling together.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，泣而對曰：「大人平生徇節義，既屬亂常，必無苟免。」

translations.literal: When asked the reason he wept and replied: "My father all his life devoted himself to integrity and righteousness; now that disorder has come, he will surely not seek a dishonorable escape."
translations.idiomatic: When asked the reason he wept and replied: "My father all his life devoted himself to integrity and righteousness; now that disorder has come, he will surely not seek a dishonorable escape."

sentences.zh: 尋而凶問果至。

translations.literal: Before long word of disaster indeed arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Before long word of disaster indeed arrived.

sentences.zh: 在喪柴毀過禮，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: In mourning he wasted his frame beyond ritual propriety; in serving his mother he was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning he wasted his frame beyond ritual propriety; in serving his mother he was famed for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 煬帝以誕死節，贈柱國、弘義郡公，令無逸襲爵。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang because Dan died for integrity enfeoffed him posthumously as Pillar of State and Duke of Hongyi commandery, and ordered Wuyi to inherit the peerage.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang because Dan died for integrity enfeoffed him posthumously as Pillar of State and Duke of Hongyi commandery, and ordered Wuyi to inherit the peerage.

sentences.zh: 時五等皆廢，以其時忠義之後，特封平輿侯。

translations.literal: At that time the five ranks were all abolished; because he was descendant of a man of loyalty and righteousness at that time, he was specially enfeoffed Marquis of Pingyu.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the five ranks were all abolished; because he was the descendant of a man of loyalty and righteousness, he was specially enfeoffed Marquis of Pingyu.

sentences.zh: 拜涓陽太守，甚有能名，差品為天下第一。

translations.literal: He was appointed Prefect of Juanyang and had a great reputation for ability; his grade ranked first under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Prefect of Juanyang and won a great reputation for ability; his grade ranked first under heaven.

sentences.zh: 再轉右武衛將軍，甚見親委。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to General of the Right Martial Guards and was greatly trusted and entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again to General of the Right Martial Guards and was greatly trusted and entrusted.

sentences.zh: 帝幸江都，以無逸留守洛陽。

translations.literal: When the emperor went to Jiangdu, he left Wuyi to guard Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to Jiangdu, he left Wuyi to guard Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 及江都之變，與段達、元文都尊立越王侗為帝。

translations.literal: When the Jiangdu upheaval occurred, he together with Duan Da and Yuan Wendu honored and established the Prince of Yue Tong as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiangdu upheaval occurred, he together with Duan Da and Yuan Wendu honored and established the Prince of Yue Tong as emperor.

sentences.zh: 王世充作難，無逸棄老母妻子，斬關而走，追騎且至，無逸曰：「吾死而後已，終不能同爾為逆。」

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong raised trouble, Wuyi abandoned his aged mother, wife, and children, cut through the passes and fled; pursuing horsemen were about to overtake him—Wuyi said: "I shall die thereafter and never join you in rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shichong raised trouble, Wuyi abandoned his aged mother, wife, and children, cut through the passes and fled; pursuing horsemen were about to overtake him—Wuyi said: "I shall die thereafter and never join you in rebellion."

sentences.zh: 因解所服金帶投之於地，曰：「以此贈卿，無為相迫。」

translations.literal: He then untied the gold belt he wore and cast it to the ground, saying: "Take this in gift to you—do not press me further."
translations.idiomatic: He then untied the gold belt he wore and cast it to the ground, saying: "Take this in gift to you—do not press me further."

sentences.zh: 追騎競下馬取帶，自相爭奪，由是得免。

translations.literal: The pursuers dismounted competing for the belt and contended with one another; on this account he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuers dismounted competing for the belt and contended with one another; on this account he escaped.

sentences.zh: 高祖以隋代舊臣，甚尊禮之，拜刑部尚書，封滑國公，歷陝東道行台民部尚書。

translations.literal: Gaozu, because he was an old minister of the Sui, treated him with great courtesy, appointing him Minister of Justice and enfeoffing him Duke of Huaguo, and he served successively as People's Minister of the Shandong Circuit Eastern Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, because he was an old minister of the Sui, treated him with great courtesy, appointing him Minister of Justice and enfeoffing him Duke of Huaguo, and he served successively as People's Minister of the Shandong Circuit Eastern Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷御史大夫。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時益部新開，刑政未洽，長吏橫恣，贓污狼藉；

translations.literal: At that time the Yi region had newly been opened; penal government was not yet harmonized—long administrators were overbearing and willful, and bribery and corruption were piled in heaps;
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Yi region had newly been opened; penal government was not yet harmonized—long administrators were overbearing and willful, and bribery and corruption were piled in heaps;

sentences.zh: 令無逸持節巡撫之，承製除授。

translations.literal: he ordered Wuyi to hold credentials and tour and pacify them, appointing and removing according to edict.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor ordered Wuyi to hold credentials and tour and pacify the region, appointing and removing officials according to edict.

sentences.zh: 無逸宣揚朝化，法令嚴肅，蜀中甚賴之。

translations.literal: Wuyi proclaimed and spread court transformation; laws and orders were stern and solemn, and Shuchuan relied greatly on him.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi proclaimed and spread court transformation; laws and orders were stern and solemn, and Shu relied greatly on him.

sentences.zh: 有皇甫希仁者，見無逸專制方面，徼幸上變，云：「臣父在洛陽，無逸為母之故，陰遣臣與王世充相知。」

translations.literal: There was one Huangfu Xiren who, seeing Wuyi monopolize power in the region, sought favor by submitting a report, saying: "My father was in Luoyang; for his mother's sake Wuyi secretly sent me to make contact with Wang Shichong."
translations.idiomatic: There was one Huangfu Xiren who, seeing Wuyi monopolize power in the region, sought favor by submitting a report, saying: "My father was in Luoyang; for his mother's sake Wuyi secretly sent me to make contact with Wang Shichong."

sentences.zh: 高祖審其詐，數之曰：「無逸逼於世充，棄母歸朕。

translations.literal: Gaozu examined his fraud and reprimanded him, saying: "Wuyi was pressed by Shichong, abandoned his mother and returned to me.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu examined his fraud and reprimanded him, saying: "Wuyi was pressed by Shichong, abandoned his mother and returned to me.

sentences.zh: 今之委任，異於眾人。

translations.literal: Today's trust in him differs from that given ordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: Today's trust in him differs from that given ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 其在益州，極為清正。

translations.literal: In Yizhou he was utterly clear and upright.
translations.idiomatic: In Yizhou he was utterly clear and upright.

sentences.zh: 此蓋群小不耐，欲誣之也。

translations.literal: This is surely petty men who cannot endure him, wishing to slander him.
translations.idiomatic: This is surely petty men who cannot endure him, wishing to slander him.

sentences.zh: 此乃離間我君臣，惑亂我視聽。」

translations.literal: This is nothing but driving wedges between emperor and minister and confusing what we see and hear."
translations.idiomatic: This is nothing but driving wedges between emperor and minister and confusing what we see and hear."

sentences.zh: 於是斬希仁於順天門，遣給事中李公昌馳往慰諭之。

translations.literal: He then executed Xiren at the Shuntian Gate and dispatched Attendant of the Imperial Secretariat Li Gongchang posthaste to comfort and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: He then executed Xiren at the Shuntian Gate and dispatched Attendant of the Imperial Secretariat Li Gongchang posthaste to comfort and instruct Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 俄而又告無逸陰與蕭銑交通者，無逸時與益州行台僕射竇璡不協，於是上表自理，又言璡罪狀。

translations.literal: Before long there was another who reported Wuyi had secretly communicated with Xiao Xian; Wuyi was then at odds with the Vice Director of the Yi Circuit Eastern Secretariat and Servitor Dou Jin—he submitted a memorial to vindicate himself and also set forth Dou's offenses.
translations.idiomatic: Before long there was another who reported that Wuyi had secretly communicated with Xiao Xian; Wuyi was then at odds with the Vice Director of the Yi Circuit Eastern Secretariat and Servitor Dou Jin—he submitted a memorial to vindicate himself and also set forth Dou's offenses.

sentences.zh: 高祖覽之曰：「無逸當官執法，無所迴避，必是邪佞之徒，惡直丑正，共相構扇也。」

translations.literal: Gaozu read it and said: "Wuyi in office enforces the law without turning aside—this must be wicked flatterers who hate the upright and resent the correct, conspiring together to slander and incite."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu read it and said: "Wuyi in office enforces the law without turning aside—this must be wicked flatterers who hate the upright and resent the true, conspiring together to slander and incite."

sentences.zh: 因令劉世龍、溫彥博將按其事，卒無驗而止，所告者坐斬，竇璡亦以罪黜。

translations.literal: He then ordered Liu Shilong and Wen Yanbo to investigate the matter; in the end nothing was verified and it stopped—the accuser was executed by law, and Dou Jin was also dismissed for his offense.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Liu Shilong and Wen Yanbo to investigate the matter; in the end nothing was verified and the case was closed—the accuser was executed, and Dou Jin was dismissed for his crimes.

sentences.zh: 無逸既返命，高祖勞之曰：「公立身行己，朕之所悉。

translations.literal: When Wuyi had returned and reported, Gaozu comforted him, saying: "Duke, in how you conduct yourself and order your life, I know you well.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuyi had returned and reported, Gaozu comforted him, saying: "Duke, in conduct and self-discipline you are a man I know well.

sentences.zh: 比多譖訴者，但為正直致邪佞所憎耳。」

translations.literal: Of late the many slanders and accusations are only because your uprightness has made the wicked and flatterers hate you, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Of late the many slanders are only because your uprightness has made the wicked and the flattering hate you, that is all.

sentences.zh: 尋拜民部尚書，累轉益州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Minister of the Ministry of Revenue and was transferred in succession to Chief Administrator of the Yi Prefecture Grand Area Commander's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Minister of the Ministry of Revenue and was transferred in succession to Chief Administrator of the Yi Prefecture Grand Area Commander's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 閉門自守，不通賓客，左右不得出門。

translations.literal: He kept his gates closed and guarded himself, not receiving guests; those at his side were not permitted to leave the house.
translations.idiomatic: He kept his gates shut and held himself apart, receiving no guests, and those around him were not allowed to go out.

sentences.zh: 凡所貨易，皆往他州；

translations.literal: whatever trade he conducted, all went to other prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: whatever trade he conducted was carried out in other prefectures;

sentences.zh: 每按部，樵採不犯於人。

translations.literal: whenever he toured his jurisdiction, woodcutters gathering fuel did not trespass on others.
translations.idiomatic: whenever he toured his jurisdiction, woodcutters gathering fuel never trespassed on others' land.

sentences.zh: 嘗夜宿人家，遇燈炷盡，主人將續之，無逸抽佩刀斷衣帶以為炷，其廉介如此。

translations.literal: Once he lodged overnight at a household; when the lamp wick was exhausted and the host was about to replace it, Wuyi drew his belt knife and cut his sash to serve as a wick—such was his integrity and austerity.
translations.idiomatic: Once he lodged overnight in a private home; when the lamp wick burned out and the host was about to replace it, Wuyi drew his belt knife and cut his sash for a wick—such was his integrity and austerity.

sentences.zh: 然過於審慎，所上表奏，懼有誤失，必讀之數十遍，仍令官屬再三披省；

translations.literal: Yet he was excessively cautious: memorials he submitted, fearing error, he would read dozens of times over and still have subordinates review them again and again;
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was excessively cautious: every memorial he submitted, fearing a mistake, he read dozens of times and still had his staff review it again and again;

sentences.zh: 使者就路，又追而更審，每遣一使，輒連日不得上道。

translations.literal: when an envoy was on the road, he would pursue and re-examine anew—each time he dispatched an envoy, the envoy could not set out for days on end.
translations.idiomatic: when an envoy was already on the road, he would pursue him and examine the matter again—each envoy he sent could not depart for days on end.

sentences.zh: 議者以此少之。

translations.literal: Critics for this reason thought somewhat less of him.
translations.idiomatic: Critics for this reason thought somewhat less of him.

sentences.zh: 母在長安疾篤，太宗令驛召之。

translations.literal: His mother in Chang'an was gravely ill; Taizong ordered her summoned by post relay.
translations.idiomatic: His mother in Chang'an was gravely ill; Taizong ordered her summoned by post relay.

sentences.zh: 無逸性至孝，承問惶懼，不能飲食，因道病卒。

translations.literal: Wuyi was by nature deeply filial; on receiving the inquiry he was fearful and distressed, could not eat or drink, and died of illness on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi was by nature deeply filial; when he received the summons he was stricken with fear and could not eat or drink, and died of illness on the road.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部尚書，太常考行，謚曰「孝」。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Rites; the Director of Ceremonies assessed his conduct and gave the posthumous name "Filial."
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites; the Director of Ceremonies assessed his conduct and gave him the posthumous name Filial.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書王珪駁之曰：「無逸入蜀之初，自當扶侍老母，與之同去，申其色養，而乃留在京師，子道未足，何得為孝？」

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Wang Gui rebutted it, saying: "When Wuyi first entered Shu he ought himself to have supported and attended his aged mother, going with her to fulfill providing comfort in her presence—yet he left her in the capital; his son's conduct was insufficient—how could he be deemed filial?
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Wang Gui objected, saying: "When Wuyi first entered Shu he ought to have supported his aged mother and gone with her, to fulfill his duty of tending her in person—yet he left her in the capital. His conduct as a son fell short—how could he be called filial?"

sentences.zh: 竟謚為良。

translations.literal: In the end his posthumous name was set as "Good."
translations.idiomatic: In the end his posthumous name was changed to Good.

sentences.zh: 孫忠，開元中為衛尉卿。

translations.literal: His grandson Zhong, in the Kaiyuan era, served as Commandant of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Zhong served as Commandant of the Guard during the Kaiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 李大亮李大亮，雍州涇陽人。

translations.literal: Li Daliang—Li Daliang was a native of Jingyang in Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Daliang was a native of Jingyang in Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 後魏度支尚書琰之曾孫也。

translations.literal: He was the great-grandson of Yanzhi, Director of Revenue in Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was the great-grandson of Yanzhi, Director of Revenue under the Later Wei.

sentences.zh: 其先本居隴西狄道，代為著姓。

translations.literal: His ancestors had originally dwelt at Didao in Longxi; generation after generation they were a prominent clan.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had originally lived at Didao in Longxi and for generations had been a family of note.

sentences.zh: 祖綱，後魏南岐州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Gang was Governor of Southern Qi Prefecture in Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gang had been Governor of Southern Qi Prefecture under the Later Wei.

sentences.zh: 父充節，隋朔州總管、武陽公。

translations.literal: His father Chongjie was Sui Commander-in-Chief of Shuozhou and Duke of Wuyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chongjie had been Sui Commander-in-Chief of Shuozhou and Duke of Wuyang.

sentences.zh: 大亮少有文武才幹，隋末，署韓國公龐玉行軍兵曹。

translations.literal: Daliang in youth had talent in civil and military affairs; at the end of Sui he was appointed acting Military Staff Officer on the campaign staff of the Duke of Han, Pang Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang in his youth showed talent in both civil and military affairs; at the end of the Sui he served as acting Military Staff Officer on the campaign staff of Pang Yu, Duke of Han.

sentences.zh: 在東都與李密戰，敗，同輩百餘人皆就死，賊帥張弼見而異之，獨釋與語，遂定交於幕下。

translations.literal: At the Eastern Capital he fought Li Mi and was defeated; more than a hundred of his companions all went to their deaths—the bandit commander Zhang Bi saw him and marveled, alone releasing him to speak, and they thus formed a bond under the tent.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Capital he fought Li Mi and was defeated; more than a hundred of his companions were put to death. The rebel commander Zhang Bi saw him and marveled, released him alone to speak with him, and they formed a bond in the camp.

sentences.zh: 義兵入關，大亮自東都歸國，授土門令。

translations.literal: When the righteous army entered the passes, Daliang from the Eastern Capital returned to the state and was appointed magistrate of Tumen.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army entered the passes, Daliang returned from the Eastern Capital to join the cause and was appointed magistrate of Tumen.

sentences.zh: 屬百姓饑荒，盜賊侵寇，大亮賣所乘馬分給貧弱，勸以墾田，歲因大稔。

translations.literal: At the time the common people suffered famine and bandits raided; Daliang sold the horse he rode and distributed the proceeds to the poor and weak, urging them to open farmland—that year there was a great harvest.
translations.idiomatic: The people were suffering famine and bandits were raiding; Daliang sold the horse he rode and distributed the proceeds among the poor, urging them to open new fields—and that year brought a great harvest.

sentences.zh: 躬捕寇盜，所擊輒平。

translations.literal: He personally captured bandits; wherever he struck, they were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He personally led raids against bandits; wherever he struck, they were subdued.

sentences.zh: 時太宗在籓，巡撫北境，聞而嗟嘆，下書勞之，賜馬一匹、帛五十段。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Qin was at his fief, touring and comforting the northern border; hearing of it he sighed in admiration, sent a written commendation, and granted one horse and fifty lengths of silk.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Prince of Qin held his fief and was touring the northern frontier; when he heard of it he sighed in admiration, sent a letter of commendation, and granted one horse and fifty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 其後，胡賊寇境，大亮眾少不敵，遂單馬詣賊營，召其豪帥，諭以禍福，群胡感悟，相率請降。

translations.literal: Afterward, when Hu bandits raided the border, Daliang's force was too few to match them; he then went alone on horseback to the bandit camp, summoned their chieftains, and instructed them on fortune and ruin—the Hu clans were moved to understanding and one after another requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Hu raiders invaded the border, Daliang's force was too small to resist; he rode alone to the enemy camp, summoned their chieftains, and spoke to them of fortune and ruin. The Hu clans were moved, and one after another they came forward to surrender.

sentences.zh: 大亮又殺所乘馬，以與之宴樂，徒步而歸。

translations.literal: Daliang again slaughtered the horse he rode and used it to feast with them, then returned on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang slaughtered the horse he had ridden and used it to feast with them, then walked home.

sentences.zh: 前後降者千餘人，縣境以清。

translations.literal: Those who surrendered before and after numbered more than a thousand; the county jurisdiction was thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand submitted in all, and the county was pacified.

sentences.zh: 高祖大悅，超拜金州總管府司馬。

translations.literal: Gaozu was greatly pleased and promoted him exceptionally to Acting Senior Administrator of the Jinzhou Area Commander's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was greatly pleased and promoted him by exception to Acting Senior Administrator of the Jinzhou Area Commander's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 時王世充遣其兄子弘烈據襄陽，令大亮安撫樊、鄧，以圖進取。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Shichong sent his elder brother's son Honglie to hold Xiangyang and ordered Daliang to pacify Fan and Deng in order to plan advance.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Shichong had sent his elder brother's son Honglie to hold Xiangyang and ordered Daliang to pacify Fan and Deng as a step toward further advance.

sentences.zh: 大亮進兵擊之，所下十餘城。

translations.literal: Daliang advanced his army to attack him and took more than ten cities.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang advanced to attack him and took more than ten cities.

sentences.zh: 高祖下書勞勉，遷安州刺史。

translations.literal: Gaozu sent a written commendation and encouragement and transferred him to Governor of An Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent a letter of commendation and transferred him to Governor of An Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 又令徇廣州巴東，行次九江，會輔公祏反，大亮以計擒公祏將張善安。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to traverse Guangzhou and Badong; on the road he reached Jiujiang and encountered Fu Gongshi's rebellion—Daliang by stratagem captured Gongshi's general Zhang Shan'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered to traverse Guangzhou and Badong; en route at Jiujiang he encountered Fu Gongshi's rebellion, and Daliang by stratagem captured Gongshi's general Zhang Shan'an.

sentences.zh: 公祏尋遣兵圍猷州，刺史左難當嬰城自守，大亮率兵進援，擊賊破之。

translations.literal: Gongshi soon sent troops to besiege You Prefecture; the governor Zuo Nandang defended the city holding fast; Daliang led troops to relieve them and struck the bandits, defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: Gongshi soon sent troops to besiege You Prefecture; Governor Zuo Nandang held the city fast; Daliang led troops to relieve him and defeated the rebels.

sentences.zh: 以功賜奴婢百人，大亮謂曰：「汝輩多衣冠子女，破亡至此，吾亦何忍以汝為賤隸乎！」

translations.literal: For his merit he was granted a hundred male and female servants; Daliang said to them: "You are mostly daughters of the gentry in robes and caps, ruined and brought to this—how could I bear to make you base slaves!"
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was granted a hundred bondsmen and bondswomen; Daliang said to them: "Most of you are daughters of families in caps and gowns, ruined and brought to this—how could I bear to make you base slaves!"

sentences.zh: 一皆放遣。

translations.literal: He released them all.
translations.idiomatic: He released them all.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞而嗟異，復賜婢二十人，拜越州都督。

translations.literal: Gaozu heard and sighed in wonder; he again granted twenty maidservants and appointed him Area Commander of Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu heard of it and marveled; he granted twenty maidservants again and appointed him Area Commander of Yue Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，轉交州都督，封武陽縣男。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan he was transferred to Area Commander of Jiao Prefecture and enfeoffed as Baron of Wuyang County.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenguan he was transferred to Area Commander of Jiao Prefecture and enfeoffed as Baron of Wuyang County.

sentences.zh: 在越州寫書百卷，及徙職，皆委之廨宇。

translations.literal: While in Yue Prefecture he copied a hundred scrolls of books; when he moved post, he left them all in the government offices.
translations.idiomatic: While in Yue Prefecture he copied a hundred scrolls of books; when he left his post, he left them all in the government offices.

sentences.zh: 尋召拜太府卿，出為涼州都督，以惠政聞。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned and appointed Director of the Palace Treasury; he went out as Area Commander of Liang Prefecture and was known for benevolent governance.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned and appointed Director of the Palace Treasury, then sent out as Area Commander of Liang Prefecture, where his benevolent governance became renowned.

sentences.zh: 嘗有台使到州，見有名鷹，諷大亮獻之。

translations.literal: Once an envoy from the central ministries came to the prefecture, saw a famous hawk, and hinted that Daliang should present it.
translations.idiomatic: Once an envoy from the central ministries came to the prefecture, saw a fine hawk, and hinted that Daliang should present it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 大亮密表曰：「陛下久絕畋獵，而使者求鷹。

translations.literal: Daliang submitted a secret memorial saying: "Your Majesty has long ceased hunting, yet the envoy requests a hawk.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang submitted a secret memorial, saying: "Your Majesty has long ceased the hunt, yet this envoy asks for a hawk.

sentences.zh: 若是陛下之意，深乖昔旨；

translations.literal: If this is Your Majesty's intent, it deeply violates your former purpose;
translations.idiomatic: If this is Your Majesty's intent, it runs deeply counter to your former resolve;

sentences.zh: 如其自擅，便是使非其人。」

translations.literal: if he acted on his own authority, then the envoy is not the right man for the mission."
translations.idiomatic: if he acted on his own authority, then he is not the right man to have been sent.

sentences.zh: 太宗下之書曰：「以卿兼資文武，志懷貞確，故委籓牧，當茲重寄。

translations.literal: Taizong sent him a letter saying: "Because you combine civil and military talent and your will is upright and firm, I have entrusted you with frontier governorship—at such a weighty charge.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent him a letter, saying: "Because you unite civil and military talent and your will is upright and firm, I entrusted you with a frontier governorship at so weighty a charge.

sentences.zh: 比在州鎮，聲績遠彰，念此忠勤，無忘寤寐。

translations.literal: While you have been in the prefecture your reputation and achievements have spread far; thinking on such loyalty and diligence, I do not forget you even in sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Since you have governed the prefecture, your reputation has spread far; when I think of such loyalty and diligence, I do not forget you even in my sleep.

sentences.zh: 使遣獻鷹，遂不曲順，論今引古，遠獻直言，披露腹心，非常懇到，覽用嘉嘆，不能便已。

translations.literal: When the envoy came to present the hawk you did not bend to accommodate him; citing the present you brought up the past, and from afar offered straight speech—laying bare your inmost heart with uncommon earnestness. Reading it I praised and exclaimed and could not soon set it aside.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy came to present the hawk you would not bend to please him; citing the present you invoked the past and offered straight counsel from afar, laying bare your inmost heart with uncommon earnestness. Reading it, I praised and exclaimed and could not soon set it down.

sentences.zh: 有臣若此，朕復何憂！

translations.literal: With a minister such as this, what have I to worry about!
translations.idiomatic: With a minister such as this, what have I to worry about!

sentences.zh: 宜守此誠，終始若一。

translations.literal: Hold to this sincerity from beginning to end as one.
translations.idiomatic: Hold to this sincerity from first to last, unchanged.

sentences.zh: 古人稱一言之重，侔於千金，卿之此言，深足貴矣。

translations.literal: The ancients said one word's weight equals a thousand in gold—your words are deeply to be treasured.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said the weight of a single word equals a thousand in gold—your words are deeply to be treasured.

sentences.zh: 今賜卿胡瓶一枚，雖無千鎰之重，是朕自用之物。」

translations.literal: Now I grant you one Hu flask; though it lacks a thousand yi in weight, it is something I use myself."
translations.idiomatic: Now I grant you one Hu flask; though it lacks the weight of a thousand yi, it is something I use myself."

sentences.zh: 又賜荀悅《漢紀》一部，下書曰：「卿立志方直，竭節至公，處職當官，每副所委，方大任使，以申重寄。

translations.literal: He also granted one copy of Xun Yue's Records of Han and sent a letter: "You set your will square and upright and exhaust your integrity to the utmost; in office you discharge every commission—about to give you great employment to fulfill this weighty trust.
translations.idiomatic: He also granted a copy of Xun Yue's Records of Han and wrote: "You set your will square and upright and exhaust your integrity to the utmost; in every office you have fulfilled what was entrusted to you. I am about to give you great employment to fulfill this weighty trust.

sentences.zh: 公事之閒，宜尋典籍。

translations.literal: In the intervals of public business you should seek out the classics.
translations.idiomatic: In the intervals of public business you should turn to the classics.

sentences.zh: 然此書敘致既明，論議深博，極為治之體，盡君臣之義，今以賜卿，宜加尋閱也。」

translations.literal: Yet this book's narrative is already clear and its discussion deep and broad—it exhausts the substance of governance and fully sets forth the meaning of ruler and minister; I now give it to you—you should apply yourself to reading it."
translations.idiomatic: This book's narrative is clear and its argument deep and broad; it exhausts the substance of good government and fully sets forth the duties of ruler and minister. I now give it to you—read it with care.

sentences.zh: 時頡利可汗敗亡，北荒諸部相率內屬。

translations.literal: At that time the Qaghan Jieli was defeated and destroyed; the northern wilds' many tribes came in succession to submit.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Qaghan Jieli was defeated and destroyed, and the tribes of the northern wastes submitted one after another.

sentences.zh: 有大度設、拓設、泥熟特勒及七姓種落等，尚散在伊吾，以大亮為西北道安撫大使以綏之，多所降附。

translations.literal: There were Dadu she, Tuoshe, the Nishu tegin, and the seven-surname clans and others still scattered at Yiwu—Daliang was made Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Circuit to soothe them, and very many submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Dadu she, Tuoshe, the Nishu tegin, and the seven-surname clans and others were still scattered at Yiwu; Daliang was made Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Circuit to soothe them, and very many submitted.

sentences.zh: 朝廷愍其部眾凍餒，遣於磧石貯糧，特加賑給。

translations.literal: The court pitied their tribes' hunger and cold and sent grain stored at Qishi for special relief distribution.
translations.idiomatic: The court pitied their tribes' hunger and cold, had grain stored at Qishi, and gave them special relief.

sentences.zh: 大亮以為於事無益，上疏曰：

translations.literal: Daliang considered it of no benefit to the affair and submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Daliang considered this of no benefit and submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 太宗納其奏。

translations.literal: Taizong accepted his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong accepted his memorial.

sentences.zh: 八年，為劍南道巡省大使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was made Touring Commissioner of the Jiannan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed Touring Commissioner of the Jiannan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 大亮激濁揚清，甚獲當時之譽。

translations.literal: Daliang stirred the foul and raised the clear and won great renown of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang stirred the foul and raised the clear, and won great renown in his day.

sentences.zh: 及討吐谷渾，以大亮為河東道行軍總管。

translations.literal: When they attacked Tuyuhun, Daliang was made Campaign Commander-in-Chief of the Hedong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When the court campaigned against Tuyuhun, Daliang was made Campaign Commander-in-Chief of the Hedong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 與大總管李靖等出北路，涉青海，歷河源，遇賊於蜀渾山，接戰破之，俘其名王，虜雜畜五萬計。

translations.literal: With the Grand Campaign Commander Li Jing and others he went out the northern route, crossed the Blue Sea, passed the River Source, met the bandits at Shuhun Mountain, joined battle and defeated them, captured their named kings, and took captives and mixed livestock numbering about fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: With Grand Campaign Commander Li Jing and others he marched by the northern route, crossed the Blue Sea and passed the River Source, met the enemy at Shuhun Mountain, joined battle and defeated them, captured their named kings, and took livestock and captives numbering about fifty thousand.

sentences.zh: 以功進爵為公，賜物千段、奴婢一百五十人，悉遺親戚。

translations.literal: For his merit his noble rank was advanced to duke; he was granted a thousand lengths of goods and a hundred fifty male and female servants—all he gave away to relatives.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit his rank was advanced to duke; he was granted a thousand bolts of goods and a hundred fifty bondsmen and bondswomen, all of which he gave to his kin.

sentences.zh: 仍罄其家資，收葬五葉宗族無後者三十餘喪，送終之禮，一時稱盛。

translations.literal: He still exhausted his family's assets, gathered and buried more than thirty coffins of his five-leaf clan with no heirs, and the rites of sending off the dead were at one time called splendid.
translations.idiomatic: He still exhausted his family's wealth, gathered and buried more than thirty coffins of kin of five generations who had left no heirs, and the funeral rites were at the time called magnificent.

sentences.zh: 後拜左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Afterward he was appointed General of the Left Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he was appointed General of the Left Guards.

sentences.zh: 十七年，晉王為皇太子，東宮僚屬，皆盛選重臣。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the Prince of Jin became Crown Prince; the Eastern Palace's staff were all richly chosen from weighty ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the Prince of Jin became Crown Prince, and the Eastern Palace staff were chosen in strength from leading ministers.

sentences.zh: 以大亮兼領太子右衛率，俄兼工部尚書，身居三職，宿衛兩宮，甚為親信。

translations.literal: Daliang was made concurrently Right Leader of the Crown Prince's Guard; soon he was also made Minister of Works—holding three offices, guarding both palaces night and day—he was deeply trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang was made concurrently Right Leader of the Crown Prince's Guard; soon he also held the Ministry of Works—holding three offices, he guarded both palaces by night and was deeply trusted.

sentences.zh: 大亮每當宿直，必通宵假寐。

translations.literal: Whenever Daliang stood night watch he always stayed awake the whole night.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Daliang stood night watch he never slept through the night.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗勞之曰：「至公宿直，我便通夜安臥。」

translations.literal: Taizong once comforted him, saying: "With you keeping watch with utmost fairness, I can sleep soundly through the night."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once comforted him, saying: "With you on watch with such utter fairness, I can sleep soundly through the night."

sentences.zh: 其見任如此。

translations.literal: Such was the trust placed in him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the trust placed in him.

sentences.zh: 太宗每有巡幸，多令居守。

translations.literal: Whenever Taizong went on tour he often had Daliang remain to guard.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Taizong went on tour he often left Daliang behind to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 房玄齡甚重之，每稱大亮有王陵、周勃之節，可以當大位。

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling greatly valued him and often said Daliang had the integrity of Wang Ling and Zhou Bo and could fill the highest position.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling greatly valued him and often said Daliang had the integrity of Wang Ling and Zhou Bo and was fit for the highest office.

sentences.zh: 大亮雖位望通顯，而居處卑陋，衣服儉率。

translations.literal: Though Daliang's status and renown were illustrious, his dwelling was humble and his clothes spare.
translations.idiomatic: Though Daliang's rank and renown were great, his dwelling was humble and his dress plain.

sentences.zh: 至性忠謹，雖妻子不見其惰容。

translations.literal: His nature was deeply loyal and careful—even wife and children never saw him slack.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was deeply loyal and careful—even his wife and children never saw him slack.

sentences.zh: 事兄嫂有同於父母。

translations.literal: He served his elder brother and sister-in-law as he would parents.
translations.idiomatic: He served his elder brother and sister-in-law as he would his parents.

sentences.zh: 每懷張弼之恩，而久不能得。

translations.literal: He always cherished Zhang Bi's kindness yet for long could not find him.
translations.idiomatic: He always cherished Zhang Bi's kindness, yet for long could not find him.

sentences.zh: 弼時為將作丞，自匿不言。

translations.literal: Bi was then Master of Palace Construction and concealed himself without speaking out.
translations.idiomatic: Bi was then Master of Palace Construction and kept himself hidden without revealing himself.

sentences.zh: 大亮嘗遇諸途而識之，持弼而泣，恨相得之晚。

translations.literal: Daliang once met him on the road and recognized him, seized Bi and wept, regretting they had found each other so late.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang once met him on the road and recognized him; he seized Bi and wept, grieving that they had found each other so late.

sentences.zh: 多推家產以遺弼，弼拒而不受。

translations.literal: He repeatedly pressed family property on Bi; Bi refused and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly pressed his family's wealth on Bi, but Bi refused to accept it.

sentences.zh: 大亮言於太宗曰：「臣有今日之榮，張弼力也。

translations.literal: Daliang said to Taizong: "The honor I have today is Zhang Bi's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang said to Taizong: "The honor I have today is Zhang Bi's doing.

sentences.zh: 有官爵請回。」

translations.literal: Whatever rank and title I have, please turn them over to him."
translations.idiomatic: Whatever rank and title I hold, I beg that they be turned over to him."

sentences.zh: 太宗遂遷弼為中郎將，俄代州都督。

translations.literal: Taizong then transferred Bi to General of the Gentlemen of the Household and soon made him Area Commander of Dai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong then promoted Bi to General of the Gentlemen of the Household and soon appointed him Area Commander of Dai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時人皆賢大亮不背恩，而多弼不自伐也。

translations.literal: People of the time all admired Daliang for not betraying kindness, and thought more of Bi for not boasting of himself.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time admired Daliang for not betraying a kindness, and admired Bi all the more for not boasting of what he had done.

sentences.zh: 十八年，太宗幸洛陽，令大亮副司空玄齡居中。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Taizong went to Luoyang and ordered Daliang to assist the Minister of Works Fang Xuanling in remaining at the center.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Taizong went to Luoyang and ordered Daliang to assist Minister of Works Fang Xuanling in remaining at the capital.

sentences.zh: 尋遇疾，太宗親為調藥，馳驛賜之。

translations.literal: Soon he fell ill; Taizong personally prepared medicine for him and sent it by post relay at full speed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he fell ill; Taizong personally prepared medicine for him and sent it posthaste by relay.

sentences.zh: 臨終上表，請停遼東之役，又言京師宗廟所在，願深以關中為意。

translations.literal: At life's end he submitted a memorial asking to halt the Liaodong campaign, and also said the capital was where the ancestral temples stood and wished they would deeply keep Guanzhong in mind.
translations.idiomatic: At life's end he submitted a memorial asking that the Liaodong campaign be halted, and also said that the capital was where the ancestral temples stood and begged that Guanzhong be kept deeply in mind.

sentences.zh: 表成而嘆曰：「吾聞禮，男子不死婦人之手。」

translations.literal: When the memorial was finished he sighed: "I have heard in the rites that a man does not die in a woman's hands."
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was finished he sighed and said: "I have heard that by the rites a man must not die in a woman's hands."

sentences.zh: 於是命屏婦人，言終而卒，時五十九。

translations.literal: He then ordered women kept away; when his words ended he died, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the women kept away; when he had finished speaking he died, at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 死之日，家無珠玉可以為唅，唯有米五石、布三十端。

translations.literal: On the day of his death the household had no pearls or jade to place in the mouth—only five shi of rice and thirty bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his death the household had no pearls or jade for the mouth-rite—only five shi of rice and thirty bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 親戚孤遺為大亮所鞠養，服之如父者十五人。

translations.literal: Orphaned relatives he had raised and cared for—fifteen wore mourning for him as for a father.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen orphaned kin he had raised wore mourning for him as for a father.

sentences.zh: 太宗為舉哀於別次，哭之甚慟，廢朝三日。

translations.literal: Taizong held mourning for him in a separate lodge and wept with great grief; he suspended court for three days.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong held mourning for him in a separate hall and wept with great grief; he suspended court for three days.

sentences.zh: 贈兵部尚書、秦州都督，謚曰懿，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of War and Area Commander of Qin Prefecture; posthumous name Yi; buried with honor at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Minister of War and Area Commander of Qin Prefecture, given the posthumous name Yi, and buried with honor at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 兄子道裕，永徽中為大理卿。

translations.literal: His elder brother's son Daoyu, in the Yonghui era, was Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother's son Daoyu served as Director of the Court of Judicial Review during the Yonghui era.

sentences.zh: 族孫迥秀迥秀，大亮族孫也。

translations.literal: Clan grandson Jiongxiu—Jiongxiu was Daliang's clan grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Clan grandson Jiongxiu was Daliang's clan grandson.

sentences.zh: 祖玄明，濟州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xuanming was Governor of Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xuanming had been Governor of Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父義本，宣州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Yiben was Governor of Xuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yiben had been Governor of Xuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 迥秀弱冠應英材傑出舉，拜相州參軍，累轉考功員外郎。

translations.literal: At the weak-crown age Jiongxiu passed the examination for Outstanding Talent and Eminent Excellence, was appointed adjutant in Xiang Prefecture, and rose in succession to Vice Director of the Bureau of Appointments in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: While still in his youth Jiongxiu passed the examination for Outstanding Talent and Eminent Excellence, received appointment as adjutant in Xiang Prefecture, and rose in succession to Vice Director of the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 則天雅愛其材，甚寵待之。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian greatly admired his talent and favored him exceedingly.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian greatly admired his ability and treated him with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 掌舉數年，遷鳳閣舍人。

translations.literal: He managed the examinations for several years and was transferred to Drafting Secretary of the Phoenix Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the civil examinations for several years, then was transferred to Drafting Secretary of the Phoenix Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 迥秀母氏庶賤而色養過人，其妻崔氏嘗叱其媵婢，母聞之不悅，迥秀即時出之。

translations.literal: Jiongxiu's mother was of lowly birth by a concubine yet in providing comfort in her presence surpassed others; his wife of the Cui clan once berated her attendants and maidservants—the mother heard of it and was displeased, and Jiongxiu at once dismissed her.
translations.idiomatic: Jiongxiu's mother, born a concubine of humble rank, yet tended her with devotion surpassing all others; when his wife Lady Cui rebuked her attendants, the mother heard of it and was displeased, and Jiongxiu at once divorced her.

sentences.zh: 或止云：「賢室雖不避嫌疑，然過非出狀，何遽如此？」

translations.literal: Someone tried to stop him, saying: "Your worthy wife, though she did not avoid arousing suspicion, yet the fault did not amount to grounds for dismissal—why so hastily?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone tried to dissuade him, saying: "Your worthy wife may have failed to avoid suspicion, yet her offense fell short of grounds for divorce—why act so hastily?"

sentences.zh: 迥秀曰：「娶妻本以承順顏色，顏色苟違，何敢留也？」

translations.literal: Jiongxiu said: "One takes a wife in order to please and tend her countenance; if that countenance is offended, how dare one retain her?"
translations.idiomatic: Jiongxiu said: "One marries to keep one's parents content; if she offends them, how dare I keep her?"

sentences.zh: 竟不從。

translations.literal: In the end he would not heed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 長安初，歷天官、夏官二侍郎，俄同鳳閣鸞台平章事。

translations.literal: In the beginning of the Chang'an era he served in succession as Vice Director of the Bureaus of Appointments and of War, and soon became Vice Chairman of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chang'an era he served in succession as Vice Director of the Bureaus of Appointments and of War, and soon became Vice Chairman of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.

sentences.zh: 則天令宮人參問其母，又嘗迎入宮中，待之甚優。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian ordered palace women to visit and inquire after his mother, and also once welcomed her into the palace, treating her with exceptional kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian sent palace women to visit and inquire after his mother, once welcomed her into the palace, and treated her with exceptional kindness.

sentences.zh: 迥秀雅有文才，飲酒斗余，廣接賓朋，當時稱為風流之士。

translations.literal: Jiongxiu was refined and possessed literary talent, drank more than a bushel of wine, widely received guests and friends, and was called at the time a man of grace and fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Refined and gifted in letters, Jiongxiu could drink more than a bushel of wine at a sitting, entertained guests and friends widely, and was acclaimed in his day as a man of grace and style.

sentences.zh: 然頗托附權幸，傾心以事張易之、昌宗兄弟，由是深為讜正之士所譏。

translations.literal: Yet he much relied on and attached himself to the favorites of power, devoting his heart to serving Zhang Yizhi and the Changzong brothers—therefore he was deeply ridiculed by upright and candid gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he relied heavily on the favorites of power, giving himself wholeheartedly to Zhang Yizhi and the Changzong brothers; for this he was deeply scorned by upright men.

sentences.zh: 俄坐贓，出為廬州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was convicted of embezzlement and left office as Governor of Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was convicted of graft and demoted to Governor of Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，累轉鴻臚卿、修文館學士，又持節為朔方道行軍大總管。

translations.literal: In the Jinglong era he rose in succession to Minister of Ceremonies and Scholar of the Cultivating Literature Hall, and also held the credential as Grand General on Campaign of the Shuofang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinglong era he rose in succession to Minister of Ceremonies and Scholar of the Cultivating Literature Hall, and also served as Grand General on Campaign for the Shuofang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 所居宅中生芝草數莖，又有貓為犬所乳，中宗以為孝感所致，使旌其門閭。

translations.literal: In his residence several stalks of auspicious fungus grew, and moreover a cat was nursed by a dog—Zhongzong considered these results of filial response and had his gate and lane honored.
translations.idiomatic: Several stalks of auspicious fungus grew at his house, and a cat was even nursed by a dog; Zhongzong took these as signs of filial virtue and ordered his gate and lane honored.

sentences.zh: 俄代姚崇為兵部尚書，病卒。

translations.literal: Soon he replaced Yao Chong as Minister of War and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he replaced Yao Chong as Minister of War and died of illness.

sentences.zh: 子齊損，開元十年，與權梁山等構逆伏誅，籍沒其家也。

translations.literal: His son Qisun—in the tenth year of Kaiyuan, together with Quan Liangshan and others plotted rebellion and was executed; his household goods were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qisun—in Kaiyuan year ten, joined Quan Liangshan and others in plotting rebellion, was executed, and his family's property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 史評史臣曰：孔子雲，「邦有道，危言危行。」

translations.literal: Historiographical appraisal—The historiographer says: Confucius said, "When the state has the Way, one's words are bold and one's conduct is cautious."
translations.idiomatic: Historiographical appraisal—The historiographer remarks: Confucius said, "When the state follows the Way, speak boldly and act with caution."

sentences.zh: 如李綱直道事人，執心不回。

translations.literal: Like Li Gang, walking the straight path in serving others, his resolve unbending.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang served others on the straight path and never bent his will.

sentences.zh: 始對隋文，慷慨獲免；

translations.literal: At first facing Emperor Wen of Sui, he spoke boldly and was spared;
translations.idiomatic: When he first confronted Emperor Wen of Sui, he spoke boldly and was spared;

sentences.zh: 終忤楊素，屈辱尤深。

translations.literal: in the end offending Yang Su, humiliation was especially deep.
translations.idiomatic: yet in the end he offended Yang Su and suffered humiliation all the deeper.

sentences.zh: 及高祖臨朝，諫舞胡鳴玉，懷不吐不茹之節，存有始有卒之規，可謂危矣。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, he remonstrated against Hu dancers with jade sounding at their belts—he bore the integrity of neither spitting nor choking, kept the principle of consistency from start to finish—one may call this precarious indeed.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, he remonstrated against Hu dancers with jade at their belts; he bore an integrity that would neither yield nor clash, and kept faith from first to last—truly living on the edge.

sentences.zh: 非逢有道，焉能免諸？

translations.literal: Had he not encountered a state with the Way, how could he have escaped?
translations.idiomatic: Had he not lived under a ruler who followed the Way, how could he have survived?

sentences.zh: 《易》曰，「王臣蹇蹇，匪躬之故」，李綱有焉。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says, "The king's minister labors in hardship—not for his own person"; Li Gang had this.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "The king's minister labors in hardship—not for his own person"—and Li Gang embodied it.

sentences.zh: 善果幼事賢母，長為正人。

translations.literal: Shanguo in youth served a worthy mother and in maturity became an upright man.
translations.idiomatic: Shanguo as a boy served a worthy mother and as a man became upright.

sentences.zh: 元璹於國有功，祗練邊事，承家不孝，終為匪人。

translations.literal: Yuanfan had merit to the state, devoted himself to mastering frontier affairs, yet in maintaining the family was unfilial and in the end became a wrongdoer.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfan served the state with merit and mastered frontier affairs, yet was unfilial toward his family and in the end became a villain.

sentences.zh: 恭仁仕隋忠厚，馭眾謙恭。

translations.literal: Gongren in Sui service was loyal and thick, in governing the masses humble and respectful.
translations.idiomatic: Gongren under the Sui was loyal and steadfast, governing his subordinates with humility.

sentences.zh: 破賊立功，方見仁者有勇；

translations.literal: In destroying bandits and achieving merit, one then saw that the benevolent have courage;
translations.idiomatic: In destroying bandits and winning merit he showed that the benevolent can be brave;

sentences.zh: 掌選被斥，所謂獨正者危。

translations.literal: in managing selection he was dismissed—what is called "the solitary upright face danger."
translations.idiomatic: in managing personnel selection he was dismissed—proving that "the solitary upright court danger."

sentences.zh: 自偽歸朝，懷才遇主，連婚帝室，列位籓宣，始終無玷者鮮矣！

translations.literal: From returning from the false [state] to the court, cherishing talent and meeting his lord, linking marriage with the imperial clan, ranking as frontier commissioner—in all this, few remained blameless from start to finish!
translations.idiomatic: From his return from the pseudo-state to court service, through talent rewarded by his lord, marriage ties with the imperial clan, and posts as frontier commissioner—few remained blameless from beginning to end!

sentences.zh: 師道慎密純善，怯懦無更事之名；

translations.literal: Shidao was cautious, solid, and pure in goodness; timid and without a name for handling affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Shidao was cautious, guileless, and thoroughly good, yet timid and without a reputation for handling affairs;

sentences.zh: 抑勢避嫌，署用致非才之誚。

translations.literal: in restraining power and avoiding suspicion, in appointments he brought on the reproach of promoting the unfit.
translations.idiomatic: in restraining powerful interests and avoiding suspicion, his appointments drew reproach for elevating unworthy men.

sentences.zh: 無逸知父守節陷難，離母避逆終吉，忠信之道著矣；

translations.literal: Wuyi knew his father held to integrity and fell into hardship, left his mother to escape rebellion and in the end met good fortune—the way of loyalty and faithfulness was manifest;
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi knew his father died holding to integrity; he left his mother to flee rebellion and in the end prospered—the Way of loyalty and faith was plain in him;

sentences.zh: 絕賓客以閉府門，斷衣帶以續燈炷，廉介之志彰矣。

translations.literal: cutting off guests to close the prefectural gate, severing his belt to keep the lamp wick burning—the aspiration of integrity and purity was displayed.
translations.idiomatic: he shut his gates to guests, tore his belt to trim a lamp wick—his integrity and austerity shone clear.

sentences.zh: 於乎，蜀道初開，親老地梗，至孝滅性，子道可知，不得謚為「孝」也，惜哉！

translations.literal: Alas! When the road to Shu first opened and his aged mother was blocked in that land, his utmost filiality consumed his being—the son's way may be known—yet he could not receive the posthumous name "Filial"—pity!
translations.idiomatic: Alas! When the road to Shu first opened, his aged mother trapped in that land, his filial devotion consumed his very life—his conduct as a son speaks for itself—yet he could not receive the posthumous name Filial—a pity indeed!

sentences.zh: 大亮文武兼才，貞確成性。

translations.literal: Daliang combined civil and military talent with firm uprightness as his nature.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang possessed both civil and military gifts, and uprightness was his nature.

sentences.zh: 賣馬勸農，是為政也；

translations.literal: Selling his horse to urge farming—that was governing;
translations.idiomatic: Selling his horse to urge the people to farm—that was statesmanship;

sentences.zh: 投身諭賊，略也；

translations.literal: throwing himself in to persuade bandits—that was daring strategy;
translations.idiomatic: throwing himself among the bandits to persuade them—that was daring strategy;

sentences.zh: 放奴婢從良者，仁也；

translations.literal: releasing slaves and bondmaids to freedom—that was benevolence;
translations.idiomatic: releasing bondmen and bondmaids to freedom—that was benevolence;

sentences.zh: 因鷹諫獵，臨終上表，忠也；

translations.literal: on account of a hawk remonstrating against the hunt, at life's end submitting a memorial—that was loyalty;
translations.idiomatic: remonstrating against the hunt because of a hawk, at life's end submitting a memorial—that was loyalty;

sentences.zh: 論伊吾之眾，智也；

translations.literal: discussing the masses at Yiwu—that was wisdom;
translations.idiomatic: counsel on the tribes at Yiwu—that was wisdom;

sentences.zh: 葬五葉無後，報張弼恩，義也；

translations.literal: burying the five-leaf kin with no heirs, repaying Zhang Bi's kindness—that was righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: burying five generations of kin who had no heirs, repaying Zhang Bi's kindness—that was righteousness;

sentences.zh: 侍兄嫂如父母，孝也；

translations.literal: serving elder brother and sister-in-law as parents—that was filial piety;
translations.idiomatic: treating his elder brother and sister-in-law as parents—that was filial piety;

sentences.zh: 不死婦人之手，禮也；

translations.literal: not dying in a woman's hands—that was ritual;
translations.idiomatic: refusing to die in a woman's hands—that was ritual propriety;

sentences.zh: 無珠玉為唅，廉也。

translations.literal: having no pearls or jade for the mouth-piece—that was integrity.
translations.idiomatic: having no pearls or jade to place in his mouth—that was integrity.

sentences.zh: 房玄齡雲，大亮有王陵、周勃之節，名下無虛士矣！

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling said that Daliang had the integrity of Wang Ling and Zhou Bo—the reputation was not an empty name for a scholar!
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling said Daliang had the integrity of Wang Ling and Zhou Bo—his reputation was no empty honor!

sentences.zh: 迥秀諂事權幸，爰至台司，余不足觀，清風替矣。

translations.literal: Jiongxiu flattered the favorites of power, rising even to the chief minister of the terrace—the rest is not worth viewing; the clear wind has been replaced.
translations.idiomatic: Jiongxiu fawned on the favorites of power until he reached the highest ministerial rank—the rest is not worth recounting; the noble tradition is gone.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：李綱守道，言行俱危。

translations.literal: Praise says: Li Gang kept the Way, words and conduct both precarious.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Li Gang kept to the Way—precarious in word and deed alike.

sentences.zh: 善果母訓，清貞是資。

translations.literal: Shanguo's mother's instruction, purity and integrity his resource.
translations.idiomatic: Shanguo—his mother's teaching; purity and integrity his foundation.

sentences.zh: 元璹父子，要道何虧。

translations.literal: Yuanfan father and son—the essential Way, what was lacking?
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfan father and son—how did they fail the essential Way?

sentences.zh: 恭仁獨正，令德無違。

translations.literal: Gongren solitary upright, admirable virtue without transgression.
translations.idiomatic: Gongren, solitary in his uprightness—admirable virtue without breach.

sentences.zh: 師道慎密，抑勢見機。

translations.literal: Shidao cautious and secret, restraining power and seeing the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao cautious and discreet, restraining power and discerning the moment.

sentences.zh: 無逸廉介，終於孝思。

translations.literal: Wuyi with integrity and purity, ending in filial reflection.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi—integrity and austerity; his end in filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 大亮才德，陵、勃名隨。

translations.literal: Daliang in talent and virtue—the names of Ling and Bo follow.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang in talent and virtue—worthy of Wang Ling and Zhou Bo.

sentences.zh: 迥秀托附，實污台司。

translations.literal: Jiongxiu relied on attachments—truly soiling the terrace ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Jiongxiu clung to the powerful—truly a stain on the highest office.
